VBO:0200759.interestingFact: The breed name is linked to Kees, a Dutch Patriot leader whose party adopted the dog as a mascot.
VBO:0200759.historicalRoots: Dutch barge companion and watchdog with spitz ancestry.

VBO:0200761.summary: Kemmer Feist is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200762.summary: Kemmer Stock Hybrid Squirrel Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200763.summary: Energetic and free-spirited, the Kerry Beagle brings a lively character to scent work. One of Ireland’s two native hounds, it stands alongside the Irish Wolfhound in the country’s canine heritage. Its pack-working tradition includes timed drag hunts; two classes in 2022 had 18 and 26 hounds running together.
VBO:0200763.shortDescription: An energetic, free-spirited Irish scent hound with a pack-working tradition that includes timed drag hunts.

VBO:0200764.summary: Keen and alert, the Kerry Blue Terrier retains the purposeful character of an Irish farm worker. It tackled vermin and could go underground after badger or otter; those demanding jobs help explain a determined streak that remains visible in its approach to a task.
VBO:0200764.shortDescription: Keen and determined, the Kerry Blue Terrier took on vermin, badger, and otter in demanding Irish farm work.
VBO:0200764.historicalRoots: Irish all-round farm and sporting terrier.

VBO:0200765.summary: King Charles Spaniels tend to be gentle and affectionate, with a happy side that can sit alongside reserve around unfamiliar people. Long prized as companions in England, these toy spaniels took their name from the dogs favored by King Charles II. Their history began with smaller spaniels related to gun dogs, even though companionship became their defining role.
VBO:0200765.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate, the King Charles Spaniel has long been prized for close companionship in England.
VBO:0200765.historicalRoots: English toy companion, historically favored by King Charles II

VBO:0200766.summary: King Charles Spaniels tend to be gentle and affectionate, with a reserved side that can coexist with a happy disposition. These companion spaniels descend from small gundogs later cherished by wealthy owners, and their name remembers King Charles II’s fondness for them.
VBO:0200766.shortDescription: A gentle, affectionate toy spaniel with a reserved side and a long history of close companionship.
VBO:0200766.historicalRoots: English and Continental toy companions developed from smaller spaniel/gundog stock; named for King Charles II.

VBO:0200767.summary: King Charles Spaniels tend to be gentle, affectionate and somewhat reserved, with a happy, intelligent manner. These English Toy Spaniels descended from small gundogs, then became treasured companions in England and on the Continent. Their name recalls a dog favoured by Charles II; later crosses with Eastern toy dogs helped shape their distinctive face.
VBO:0200767.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate with a little reserve, this English Toy Spaniel recalls a royal companion.

VBO:0200768.summary: Gentle and affectionate, the Ruby King Charles Spaniel is a happy toy companion that can be reserved rather than immediately outgoing. Its royal name was retained at King Edward VII’s urging. In 1945 the Kennel Club separated King Charles and Cavalier spaniels, keeping this compact toy branch distinct; Ruby is one of its four maintained colours.
VBO:0200768.shortDescription: A gentle, affectionate royal toy spaniel with a reserved streak; Ruby is one of four maintained colours.

VBO:0200769.summary: An affectionate, gentle companion with a reserved streak, the Tricolour King Charles Spaniel belongs to the same royal toy-spaniel breed as the Ruby. Toy spaniels were treasured as pets in England and on the Continent; their history reaches back to little gundogs. Today the Tricolour remains one of four colour varieties under a shared standard.
VBO:0200769.shortDescription: An affectionate, gently reserved toy companion; Tricolour belongs to the royal spaniels’ shared pet history.

VBO:0200770.summary: The King Shepherd tends to be watchful and devoted to its people, with an exuberant streak and a willingness to work. Its intended roles span companionship, guarding and sheep herding. A ground-covering trot gives this substantial shepherd an economical way to keep moving.
VBO:0200770.shortDescription: A watchful, devoted working shepherd with an exuberant streak and an easy, ground-covering trot.

VBO:0200771.summary: King's White Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200772.summary: Watchful and quick to learn, the Kintamani-Bali Dog tends to be gentle and loyal with familiar people. It comes from the highlands around Sukawana, where it has been kept as a close household companion. That mountain-village history is clear even though the breed’s earliest ancestry remains uncertain.
VBO:0200772.shortDescription: Watchful and quick to learn, the Kintamani-Bali Dog is loyal with familiar people and rooted in highland village life.

VBO:0200773.summary: Kirhiz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200774.summary: The Kishu Ken tends to be alert, enduring, faithful and responsive, traits useful when tracking and confronting wild boar. It was shaped in Japan’s Kishu mountains for hunting, now especially wild boar. The breed’s regional identity was formally honored in Japan as a natural monument in 1934.
VBO:0200774.shortDescription: Alert and responsive, the Kishu Ken brings endurance and fidelity to boar hunting in Japan’s Kishu mountains.
VBO:0200774.historicalRoots: Kishu mountain hunter used mainly for wild boar.

VBO:0200775.summary: Kleiner Münsterländers often work with alert friendliness and close attention to their people. In the field they bring persistence and a strong interest in game, with a tradition of searching, pointing and retrieving across woodland, open ground and water. Their development in northern Germany’s Münsterland is documented from the late nineteenth century.
VBO:0200775.shortDescription: Friendly and attentive in company, this Münsterland hunter searches, points and retrieves across land and water.

VBO:0200776.summary: Kleiner Münsterländer Vorstehund is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200777.summary: Lively and cheerful, the Kokoni combines a loyal companion’s character with an alert side. In Greece it has also been used to sound the alarm and watch small domestic animals. Those modest guarding duties sit alongside companionship in a breed found across the country.
VBO:0200777.shortDescription: A lively, cheerful Greek companion with an alert side, also used to watch small domestic animals.

VBO:0200778.summary: Kombai dogs observed in Tamil Nadu’s Theni district showed watchfulness toward strangers and responsiveness to familiar handlers. Named for a local village, this regional type has been kept for guarding homes and property; its strongest recorded tradition is protection close to the household.
VBO:0200778.shortDescription: In a Theni district study, Kombai dogs were watchful toward strangers and responsive to familiar handlers, fitting local guarding work.

VBO:0200779.summary: Decisive and distrustful of intruders, the Komondor tends to keep a particularly active watch after dark. Hungarian livestock guardians had to judge threats to a flock or property and act without constant direction. That independent night-guarding rhythm shaped the breed’s enduring character.
VBO:0200779.shortDescription: Decisive and independently watchful, the Komondor keeps an especially active night guard around flocks and property.
VBO:0200779.interestingFact: The Komondor’s ancestors are associated with Magyar pastoral movements into the Carpathian Basin.

VBO:0200780.summary: Koochee Sage is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200782.summary: Alert and eager to work with its handler, the Koolie tends to put its herding instinct to practical use. It can gather sheep or cattle, move a group in a chosen direction, or hold stock together while waiting for instructions. Australian breeders have long selected for field performance, with somewhat different lines serving open paddocks, yards and livestock trucks.
VBO:0200782.shortDescription: An alert, handler-focused Australian herder whose instinct is to gather, move or hold livestock as a working team.

VBO:0200785.summary: Quick to sound a forceful warning at unfamiliar people or animals, the Koyun dog is a regional flock guardian of Turkey’s eastern Black Sea uplands. It also guards its owner’s property and belongings. Found around Rize and Ordu, it has strong legs suited to the steep Canik hills, where sheep, goats and cattle are raised.
VBO:0200785.shortDescription: An eastern Black Sea flock guardian, known for strong warning barks and work around its owner’s animals and property.

VBO:0200786.summary: The Kromfohrländer tends to be spirited, adaptable and docile, sometimes reserved with strangers and usually showing only a modest hunting instinct. It was developed near Siegen, Germany, as a companion rather than a specialist hunter. The breed’s unusual name comes from the local Krom Fohr district, home to its first breeder.
VBO:0200786.shortDescription: Spirited and adaptable, the Kromfohrländer was developed as a companion and generally has only a modest hunting instinct.
VBO:0200786.historicalRoots: German companion breed developed near Siegen in the mid-twentieth century.

VBO:0200787.summary: Kuchi is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200788.summary: Kugsha Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200789.summary: Kui Mlk is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200790.summary: Kumaon Mastiff is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200791.summary: Kunming Wolfhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200792.summary: Kurī is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200793.summary: Brave and self-confident, the Kuvasz was trusted to protect Hungarian flocks and property even when people were out of reach. Its devotion to a charge grew from that independent guardian role; the breed also appeared at the court of King Matthias Corvinus, where it could accompany hunts.
VBO:0200793.shortDescription: Brave and self-confident, the Kuvasz guarded Hungarian flocks and property even when people were out of reach.

VBO:0200794.summary: Kyi-Apso is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200795.summary: Lively, affectionate and responsive, the Kyi-Leo is described as a trusting, loyal companion. Its breed standard also emphasizes a calm, gentle manner. The breed developed from Lhasa Apso–Maltese stock, with Harriet Linn organizing its development from 1965 and working with other kennels before formalization in the 1970s.
VBO:0200795.shortDescription: A lively, loyal companion from Lhasa Apso–Maltese stock, with a breed standard that prizes responsiveness and a gentle manner.

VBO:0200796.summary: Still a handful at twelve months, La-Chon Josh offers a personal glimpse of this Lhasa Apso–Bichon Frise cross. His owner recalls that he learned to sit, offer a paw and lie down by four months, with food helping simple lessons. At seven months, he entered a willful stage: when other dogs were around, he wanted to play and ignored recall even when a treat was offered.
VBO:0200796.shortDescription: A Lhasa Apso–Bichon cross; Josh’s early story pairs food-motivated learning with a willful, play-distracted recall stage.

VBO:0200797.summary: Playful and fond of squeaky toys, Georgie is described by Animal House Shelter as a Labrador–Shar-Pei mix that also enjoys cuddles and food rewards. Parkland Humane Society describes its young Lab Pei Maree as outgoing, keen on attention and vocal. The Lab Pei name refers to a Labrador Retriever–Shar-Pei cross.
VBO:0200797.shortDescription: In Animal House Shelter’s account, Georgie, identified as a Labrador–Shar-Pei mix, is playful and fond of toys and cuddles.

VBO:0200798.summary: The Labradoodle’s early story is one of carefully selected guide work. In 1989, Wally Conron crossed a Labrador with a Standard Poodle while seeking a guide dog for a woman in Hawaii whose husband had allergies. Sultan, one of three puppies, was chosen for his temperament and went on to guide her; the cross then found a much wider companion following.
VBO:0200798.shortDescription: A Labrador–Poodle cross with a guide-dog origin story: Sultan was selected for temperament and trained for a woman in Hawaii.
VBO:0200798.historicalRoots: Labrador–Poodle guide-dog breeding at the Royal Guide Dogs Association of Australia in 1989.

VBO:0200799.summary: Labrador Huskies work in teams pulling sleds through snowy trails. At Northern Lights Dog Sledding, the dogs carry visitors along portage routes and across Lake Melville. For owner Scott Hudson’s family, keeping these dogs continues an Inuit–Métis tradition rooted in the coastal community of Black Tickle.
VBO:0200799.shortDescription: A Labrador sled-dog type with a coastal family tradition and documented team work on snowy trails.

VBO:0200800.summary: Labrador Retrievers tend to be outgoing, cooperative and strongly motivated to work with people. A keen nose, enthusiasm for water and a gentle carrying grip are central to their retrieving skills. Their story links working dogs on the Newfoundland coast with British gundog development, where retrieving trials helped establish the breed’s reputation.
VBO:0200800.shortDescription: Outgoing and cooperative, the Labrador brings a keen nose, enthusiasm for water, and a gentle grip to retrieving.
VBO:0200800.historicalRoots: Newfoundland water-dog roots; developed as a retriever in Great Britain.

registryGroups.label: Group 8 · Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs

VBO:0200801.summary: TSA’s EEbbers loved squeaky toys, swimming and attention from strangers. This Vizsla–Labrador Retriever cross grew up in TSA’s puppy program and worked security at two Super Bowls and the Special Olympics World Games, before retiring in 2022.
VBO:0200801.shortDescription: A Vizsla–Labrador Retriever cross with EEbbers’ documented love of toys and swimming, plus event-security work.

VBO:0200803.summary: Affectionate and fond of offering a paw, two-year-old Alex gives a rescue’s account of the Labstaff, a Staffordshire Bull Terrier–Labrador cross. Rescue Remedies described him as calm and well-mannered indoors, a keen runner and a comfortable car traveller. Sudden movements or noises could still spook him.
VBO:0200803.shortDescription: Alex’s rescue account describes an affectionate Labstaff who offered a paw, settled indoors and travelled well by car.

VBO:0200805.summary: Laika is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200807.summary: Lakelands tend to be bold, friendly and self-confident, quick to notice what happens around them. Their lively expectation has a practical history: farmers in England’s Lake District developed these terriers to pursue foxes that threatened sheep across the rocky fells.
VBO:0200807.shortDescription: Bold and friendly, the Lakeland Terrier was shaped to pursue foxes across the rocky fells where sheep were at risk.

VBO:0200808.summary: Cheerful and affectionate with familiar people, the Lancashire Heeler also keeps a quick eye out for small quarry. It worked cattle in northwest England and turned the same brisk attention to rats and rabbits around the farm. Its exact ancestry remains uncertain, but that dual cattle-and-vermin role is well documented.
VBO:0200808.shortDescription: Cheerful and affectionate, the Lancashire Heeler worked cattle and turned the same quick attention to farm vermin.
VBO:0200808.interestingFact: Its proposed ancestry includes Welsh cattle dogs and Manchester Terriers, though the exact history remains unproven.
VBO:0200808.historicalRoots: Lancashire cattle and farm vermin work.

VBO:0200809.summary: Landseer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200810.summary: Self-confident and even-tempered, Landseers often form strong attachments to their people while keeping watch over home. Their affinity for water has also taken them into rescue work, while the European Continental breed’s guard-and-companion role traces to Germany and Switzerland.
VBO:0200810.shortDescription: Self-confident and even-tempered, this watchful companion has strong ties to people and a notable love of water.
VBO:0200810.historicalRoots: European Continental Landseer developed in Germany and Switzerland from the old white-and-black Newfoundland lineage.

VBO:0200811.summary: Landseer Newfoundland is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200813.summary: Lapphund is a dog breed or regional type associated with Finland.

VBO:0200814.summary: The Lapponian Herder may bark readily while working yet often remains calm, friendly and willing in other settings. Sámi herders used dogs of this tradition to move reindeer, a job that rewards a steady pace and close attention to the herd. Finnish breeders later distinguished it from the Finnish Lapphund as a separate reindeer-working type.
VBO:0200814.shortDescription: Calm and willing away from work, the Lapponian Herder may bark readily while moving reindeer with Sámi herders.
VBO:0200814.historicalRoots: Sámi reindeer-herding dog of northern Finland.

VBO:0200815.summary: Lapponian Shepherd is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200816.summary: The Large Münsterländer is often lively without nervousness and readily taught, a temperament suited to close teamwork with a hunter. It searches field, forest and water, points game and retrieves after the shot; its distinct breed line endured after black dogs were excluded from another German pointing register.
VBO:0200816.shortDescription: Lively without nervousness, the Large Münsterländer searches, points, and retrieves across field, forest, and water.
VBO:0200816.historicalRoots: German versatile pointing and retrieving dog.

VBO:0200817.summary: Larson Lakeview Bulldogge is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200818.summary: Latvian Hounds tend to be sociable, good-natured and energetic, with a strong hunting drive. They were bred to hunt both small game and hoofed animals, using ground and air scent. After wartime mixing nearly erased the earlier Courland hound, selective breeding established the Latvian Hound in 1971.
VBO:0200818.shortDescription: A sociable, energetic Latvian hound with a strong hunting drive and a history of tracking varied game.

VBO:0200819.summary: Composed and playful around familiar people, the Leonberger became a steady companion and watch dog. Heinrich Essig developed it near Stuttgart in the nineteenth century, drawing on several giant working breeds. Its calm manner amid busy household life has remained central to the breed’s identity.
VBO:0200819.shortDescription: Composed and playful with familiar people, the Leonberger became a steady companion and watch dog.
VBO:0200819.historicalRoots: Nineteenth-century German giant companion and watchdog.

VBO:0200820.summary: Leopard Cur is a dog breed or regional type associated with United States.

VBO:0200821.summary: Levesque is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200822.summary: Levriero Sardo is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200823.summary: Food, treats and hour-long belly rubs were favorites of Ta-shi, a Lha-Cocker whose keeper described her at seven months old. This Lhasa Apso–Cocker Spaniel cross was also called intelligent and protective of the small circle of creatures she accepted.
VBO:0200823.shortDescription: A Lhasa Apso–Cocker Spaniel cross; seven-month-old Ta-shi’s keeper described a fondness for food, treats and long belly rubs.

VBO:0200824.summary: The Lhasa Apso tends to be alert and self-possessed, sometimes keeping a little distance from strangers while remaining steady with its own circle. It was shaped by Tibet’s high-altitude climate and later reached Britain in the 1920s. Early British fanciers confused it with other shaggy Tibetan dogs before recognizing the Apso separately.
VBO:0200824.shortDescription: Alert and self-possessed, the Lhasa Apso tends to be steady with its own circle and more distant with strangers.
VBO:0200824.historicalRoots: Tibetan highland companion; introduced to Britain in the 1920s.

VBO:0200825.summary: Affectionate and sociable on neighborhood walks, adult Lhasa-Poo Duffer gives a personal glimpse of this Lhasa Apso–Poodle cross. His owner describes meeting neighborhood dog friends and a love of petting and lap time. He is also vocal about daily routines: he alerts her to visitors and passersby, and barks when he wants permission to climb onto a lap or the foot of her bed.
VBO:0200825.shortDescription: A Lhasa Apso–Poodle cross; adult Duffer enjoys neighborhood dog friends, petting and vocal reminders of daily routines.

VBO:0200827.summary: Valued by local hunters for its scent-hunting ability, the Liangshan Dog is a regional mountain hound of western Sichuan in China. Endurance is among its described working strengths in rugged terrain, where it belongs to a local hunting tradition.
VBO:0200827.shortDescription: A western Sichuan scent hunter, valued locally for mountain hunting and described as an enduring working hound.

VBO:0200828.summary: Limer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200829.summary: Good-natured yet energetic and persistent on a trail, the Lithuanian Hound combines endurance with a melodious, changing voice. Its work includes finding fresh game tracks and following wounded animals, tasks that draw on keen scent and good orientation. The modern breed was rebuilt from surviving local hounds beginning in 1957–58, with a first provisional standard in 1966.
VBO:0200829.shortDescription: An energetic, good-natured Lithuanian hound with a melodious voice, persistent tracking and a strong sense of direction.

VBO:0200830.summary: Lively and people-oriented, the Llewellin Setter combines a desire for human attention with strong field instincts. It belongs to the performance strain descended from Purcell Llewellin's nineteenth-century English Setters, selected to locate and point upland birds. In 2021, UKC said it would retain the Field Dog Stud Book’s rules and DNA checks for registration under the Llewellin name.
VBO:0200830.shortDescription: A lively, people-oriented setter from a documented performance strain, selected to locate and point upland birds.

VBO:0200831.summary: Lobito Herreño is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200832.summary: Long-Haired Pyrenean Sheepdogs are lively, resourceful herders with a habit of taking initiative. Their attachment to the shepherd comes with a headstrong streak and caution toward strangers. They developed in the French Pyrenees, where small, quick dogs worked across mountain pastures.
VBO:0200832.shortDescription: Quick and resourceful on mountain pasture, this Pyrenean herder takes initiative and bonds closely with its shepherd.
VBO:0200832.historicalRoots: Pyrenean mountain herding dog, long-haired variety
editorialFamilies: Pyrenean mountain herding dog, long-haired variety

VBO:0200833.summary: Affectionate and sociable, the Long-Haired Whippet combines the intensity of a sighthound with an unusually responsive approach to working with people. Coursing, agility and scentwork are among its modern activities. Developed in the United States from the 1960s, this distinct coated breed adopted the name Windsprite in 2017.
VBO:0200833.shortDescription: A sociable, responsive coated sighthound, the Windsprite brings athletic intensity to coursing and agility.

VBO:0200834.summary: Loughlander is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200835.summary: Serious and businesslike at work but sometimes clownish at home, the Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog has been used to track game and bay feral hogs and cattle. The breed can be independent and protective while also affectionate with familiar people; Louisiana named it the state dog in 1979.
VBO:0200835.shortDescription: Businesslike in the field and sometimes clownish at home, this Louisiana worker can be independent and loyal.
VBO:0200835.historicalRoots: A Louisiana multipurpose working dog used for game and stock; its deeper origins are uncertain, and it became Louisiana’s state dog in 1979.

VBO:0200836.summary: Affectionate and attentive, the Löwchen tends to watch people closely and can settle quietly when asked. European courts long kept it as a companion, and historical art preserves its presence there; its social responsiveness is the skill behind a breed whose working day unfolded beside people.
VBO:0200836.shortDescription: Affectionate and attentive, the Löwchen watches people closely and can settle quietly, reflecting centuries as a court companion.

VBO:0200837.summary: Friendly, willing and active, the Lucas Terrier is a sturdy small dog developed for terrier work. Sir Jocelyn Lucas began the line in the 1940s by crossing a Norfolk Terrier with one of his Ilmer Sealyhams. The original club continues to preserve those Ilmer bloodlines through a small breeding programme.
VBO:0200837.shortDescription: A friendly, willing and active small working terrier whose club preserves Sir Jocelyn Lucas's original Ilmer bloodlines.

VBO:0200838.summary: Alert and energetic, the Norwegian Lundehund carries an unusual climbing heritage. On Norway’s steep coastal rocks, these dogs once entered narrow puffin burrows; extra functional toes, folding ears and remarkable flexibility helped with that work. The birds are protected today, so the breed’s old job belongs to its history.
VBO:0200838.shortDescription: An agile coastal climber, the Lundehund once entered narrow puffin burrows using extra toes and unusual flexibility.

VBO:0200839.summary: Lively, proud and independent, the Lupo Italiano tends to form close bonds with its people while remaining reserved with strangers. Its association describes a versatile search dog that follows ground trails and scent carried on the air, including in mountain rescue. Mario Messi began developing the population in 1966.
VBO:0200839.shortDescription: A lively, independent Italian search dog, closely attached to its people and used for ground and air scent work.

VBO:0200840.summary: Affectionate and often sensitive, Lurchers tend to enjoy close company, though their energy and confidence vary. Many have a strong instinct to chase and enjoy short bursts of running before relaxing at home. A Lurcher is a sighthound crossed with another dog type, so this name covers many different combinations.
VBO:0200840.shortDescription: A varied sighthound-cross type, often affectionate and sensitive, with a strong chase instinct in many dogs.

VBO:0200841.summary: Mackenzie River Husky is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200843.summary: Mahratta Greyhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200844.summary: Under its NKC standard, the Majestic Tree Hound is affectionate and sensitive to kindness or correction. Two-year-old Bull sought attention from anyone who offered it; his keeper described littermate Tank as intelligent and independent. The pair enjoyed country roaming and lawn lounging, but also chased deer for miles.
VBO:0200844.shortDescription: Affectionate in the NKC standard, with Bull’s attention-seeking and Tank’s independent roaming and deer chasing.

VBO:0200845.summary: Ca de Bou dogs tend to be quiet and self-assured with familiar people, but become sharply watchful when roused. Their history runs from guarding Balearic coastal settlements to bull baiting, which gave the breed its name: “bull dog.”
VBO:0200845.shortDescription: Quiet and self-assured with familiar people, the Ca de Bou becomes keenly watchful when roused.
VBO:0200845.historicalRoots: Mallorcan mastiff used in cattle and property work; historical bull-spectacle use documented.

VBO:0200846.summary: The Majorca Ratter tends to be lively and affectionate, with an excitable streak. Around Mallorcan homes, its watchfulness has shared space with a practical talent for hunting rats and rabbits. Quick strides and strong hindquarters help it leap nimbly.
VBO:0200846.shortDescription: A lively, affectionate Mallorcan rat-and-rabbit hunter, also known for keeping watch around the home.

VBO:0200847.summary: Majorca Shepherd Dogs tend to be affectionate and strongly attached to their own person, yet reserved with strangers; that reserve can be especially marked when young. On Mallorca, their working life centered on herding flocks and guarding property.
VBO:0200847.shortDescription: Affectionate with its person and reserved with strangers, this Mallorcan shepherd tended flocks and guarded property.
VBO:0200847.historicalRoots: Mallorcan herding, guarding and farm defense dog; short coat most common of two varieties.

VBO:0200848.summary: Affectionate and strongly attached to its own person, the long-haired Majorca Shepherd shares the breed’s reserve toward strangers. Known as the Ca Cabrer, it is an officially described coat variety of Mallorca’s Ca de Bestiar. These dogs have worked with sheep and goats as well as other farm animals, combining pastoral work with guarding; their characteristic working gait is a gallop.
VBO:0200848.shortDescription: The long-haired Ca de Bestiar shares the breed’s attachment to its keeper and its history of pastoral work and guarding.

VBO:0200849.summary: Majorca Shepherd Dogs are intelligent and affectionate toward their person while often reserved with strangers. They were bred on the Balearic Islands for shepherding, guarding and defense, work that calls for a close response to a familiar handler and watchfulness around newcomers. The shorthaired form is the more common of two varieties.
VBO:0200849.shortDescription: An intelligent, watchful Balearic shepherd and guard dog; this is its common shorthaired form.
VBO:0200849.historicalRoots: Balearic island shepherding and guarding tradition.

VBO:0200851.summary: Veterinarian Stuart Fitzgerald describes the Mal-Shi as cheerful, alert and affectionate, thriving on human company. His account notes an interest in new visitors, ball games and exploring a garden. This is the Maltese–Shih Tzu companion cross.
VBO:0200851.shortDescription: A Maltese–Shih Tzu cross described by veterinarian Stuart Fitzgerald as cheerful, affectionate and keen on company.

VBO:0200856.summary: Lively and affectionate near its people, the Maltese has long filled a close companion role around the Mediterranean. Maritime settlements figure in its history, though the exact route of its origins remains debated. Even its name carries a mystery, perhaps echoing an old word for harbor rather than referring only to Malta.
VBO:0200856.shortDescription: Lively and affectionate near its people, the Maltese has filled a close companion role around the Mediterranean for centuries.

VBO:0200857.summary: Maltese – Teacup is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200858.summary: Affectionate once familiar, Mocha was a Maltese–Jack Russell cross whose rescuers said relationships took time to form. They described an active dog who loved playing with younger small dogs, learned new routines quickly and responded to food rewards and commands. The same account noted barking when people tried to leave.
VBO:0200858.shortDescription: Mocha’s rescuers described a lively Maltese–Jack Russell cross, affectionate once familiar and keen on food rewards.

VBO:0200859.summary: Maltese Terrier is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200860.summary: Closely attached to their people, Maltipoos can be vocal, barking when they notice unfamiliar sights or sounds. This named cross combines a Maltese with a Toy or Miniature Poodle. Regular brushing and professional grooming are part of keeping its coat in good order.
VBO:0200860.shortDescription: A people-attached Maltese–Poodle cross with a vocal streak around unfamiliar sights and sounds.

VBO:0200861.summary: Playful and adventurous, Bear was a nine-year-old Maltipom whose keeper said she enjoyed exploring outdoors and snuggling on the couch for belly rubs. Food rewards helped her learn sit, stay and “drop it.” The same account described an alert dog who could bark excessively and occasionally become snappy.
VBO:0200861.shortDescription: Bear’s keeper described a playful Maltipom who enjoyed outdoor exploring, couch snuggles and learning with food rewards.

VBO:0200862.summary: The Manchester Terrier tends to be keen and alert, yet discerning and devoted in close company. It earned its name in an English city where ratting contests and pub shows helped make it a recognizable breed. The city’s ratting culture gave this keen little terrier a practical nineteenth-century job.
VBO:0200862.shortDescription: Keen and alert yet devoted in company, the Manchester Terrier carries a ratting history from its namesake English city.

VBO:0200864.summary: Independent and strong-willed, the Maneto seeks company and affection while taking a keen interest in its territory. This southern Andalusian rabbit dog follows scent through dense Mediterranean scrub and retrieves game, including from water. Its low, sturdy build helps it reach tight cover.
VBO:0200864.shortDescription: An independent rabbit tracker from southern Andalusia, drawn to company and persistent work in dense scrub.

VBO:0200865.summary: Perceptive and devoted to its charge, the Maremma Sheepdog has long guarded flocks in central Italy. Seasonal movement between the Abruzzo mountains and Maremma lowlands brought two regional working strains together; the dog had to stay alert to danger through the shepherd's long journeys.
VBO:0200865.shortDescription: Perceptive and devoted to its charge, the Maremma Sheepdog guarded flocks through seasonal moves across central Italy.
VBO:0200865.historicalRoots: Italian Abruzzo and Maremma flock-protection dog.

VBO:0200866.summary: Marquesan Dog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200867.summary: Calm and affectionate with familiar people, the Mastiff also retains the watchful courage of Britain’s long guard-dog tradition. Accounts of mastiff-type dogs reach back before Agincourt, but the breed’s present-day manner is often quiet and self-possessed. Its ability to notice a threat without constant agitation is a less visible part of its guardian character.
VBO:0200867.shortDescription: Quiet and affectionate with familiar people, the Mastiff retains watchful courage from Britain’s long guard-dog tradition.

VBO:0200870.summary: Affectionate and eager to please, two-year-old Racket illustrates one keeper’s account of a Mastweiler. Her owner described an alert dog who guarded when voices rose angrily, yet enjoyed rough play with their English Bull Terrier. Racket came from a multigeneration programme based largely on English Mastiffs and Rottweilers, with a reported distant Neapolitan Mastiff ancestor whose exact place in the pedigree was uncertain.
VBO:0200870.shortDescription: A Mastiff–Rottweiler cross; Prince’s owner described camping and river trips, while Racket’s noted eager affection.

VBO:0200871.summary: Mazandarani Sage is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200872.summary: Loyal to its handler and sometimes reserved at first meetings, the McNab Shepherd is described by its foundation as eager to work. Its herding style is upright and loose-eyed: it goes to the head of livestock to gather and hold them. A keen nose helps locate stock hidden in brush.
VBO:0200872.shortDescription: A loyal working stockdog, gathering livestock with an upright, loose-eyed style and finding hidden animals by scent.

VBO:0200874.summary: Meliteo Kinidio is a dog breed or regional type associated with Greece.

VBO:0200875.summary: Often sweet-natured and adaptable, the Mi-Ki was developed as a companion dog. Mikki Mackin began its breeding program in Wisconsin, aiming for a calm, quiet nature. The original dogs brought together Shih Tzu ancestry and several other toy-dog lines before later breeders continued developing the companion breed.
VBO:0200875.shortDescription: A sweet-natured companion developed from several toy-dog lines, with calmness among its breeders’ aims.

VBO:0200876.summary: Middle Asian Ovtcharka is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200878.summary: Miniature Alaskan Husky is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200879.summary: Alert and keen to learn, the Miniature American Eskimo Dog is an attentive companion whose warning bark often announces a visitor. It may be reserved at first with strangers while engaging readily with its people. The miniature is the middle of three maintained sizes, all sharing one breed standard.
VBO:0200879.shortDescription: An alert, quick-learning companion in the middle Eskimo size, often vocal about visitors and reserved at first.

VBO:0200880.summary: Devoted and energetic, the Miniature American Shepherd tends to be watchful with strangers and eager to work with familiar people. Developed from smaller Australian Shepherds in California, it kept a strong herding instinct and approaches tasks with persistence and lively attention.
VBO:0200880.shortDescription: Devoted and energetic, the Miniature American Shepherd keeps a persistent herding instinct and watches unfamiliar arrivals.
VBO:0200880.historicalRoots: Developed in California from smaller Australian Shepherds for ranch work.

VBO:0200882.summary: Miniature Bull Terriers tend to greet life with fearless playfulness and a stubborn streak; they can be amusingly determined while remaining people-oriented. Their British line fell so far out of favor that it left the Kennel Club register in 1918, before enthusiasts revived it in 1938.
VBO:0200882.shortDescription: Fearlessly playful and sometimes stubborn, the Miniature Bull Terrier can be amusingly determined in close company.
VBO:0200882.historicalRoots: Smaller British Bull Terrier line revived in 1938 after earlier decline.

VBO:0200883.summary: Miniature Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200884.summary: Sociable and often eager for company, Cockapoos can enjoy learning, games and close involvement with their people; some become unsettled when left alone. The miniature version traces its size to Miniature Poodle ancestry, paired originally with a Cocker Spaniel. Working or show Cocker ancestry and later generations bring variation in energy, temperament and coat, even within a litter.
VBO:0200884.shortDescription: A company-loving Cocker–Miniature Poodle cross whose energy, coat and temperament vary with its ancestry.

VBO:0200885.summary: Miniature Doberman Pinscher is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200886.summary: Miniature English Bull Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200887.summary: Miniature Bull Terriers are spirited, fun-loving companions whose resolve can show as stubbornness. The miniature line was removed from Britain’s breed register in 1918, then enthusiasts revived it with a dedicated club in 1938. The standard still asks for an even temperament and a response to discipline.
VBO:0200887.shortDescription: A spirited, fun-loving small terrier whose determined nature can sometimes become obstinate.
VBO:0200887.historicalRoots: Nineteenth-century British miniature Bull Terrier line revived in 1938.

VBO:0200888.summary: Miniature Bull Terriers are spirited and courageous, often pairing a fun-loving streak with an obstinate side. The smaller Bull Terrier type was known in the early 1800s, then fell from the Kennel Club register in 1918. Enthusiasts formed a club and revived the breed in 1938.
VBO:0200888.shortDescription: Spirited and fun-loving, this smaller Bull Terrier survived an early decline through a 1938 revival.

VBO:0200889.summary: Bold, inquisitive and eager to learn, the Miniature Fox Terrier is an animated little hunter with a quick spring and an abrupt change of direction. Australian Mini Foxies worked around farm homesteads controlling vermin. The Mini Foxie Club formed in 1986 to preserve that population and still maintains its own standard and registry.
VBO:0200889.shortDescription: A bold, inquisitive Australian homestead terrier, quick to spring into a chase and eager to learn.

VBO:0200890.summary: Friendly, confident dogs that readily engage with people are the Goldendoodle association’s breeding aim for every size. The Miniature Goldendoodle is a smaller Golden Retriever–Poodle companion cross. Active play is part of the standard’s picture, alongside a light, flowing trotting gait.
VBO:0200890.shortDescription: A smaller Golden Retriever–Poodle companion cross, bred toward friendly confidence and an active, playful character.

VBO:0200891.summary: Miniature Jack Russell Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200892.summary: In one UK owner survey, Labradoodles were more excitable than Labradors but had fewer separation-related problems than Poodles. The miniature version draws its size from Miniature Poodle ancestry within the original Labrador–Poodle cross. It is distinct from the separately developed Australian Labradoodle, whose ancestry includes several additional breeds.
VBO:0200892.shortDescription: A Labrador–Miniature Poodle cross with variable temperament, distinct from the developed Australian Labradoodle.

VBO:0200893.summary: The Miniature Pinscher is a German companion pinscher with a lively, self-assured temperament. It tends to be quick to notice its surroundings, spirited in activity and even in familiar company. German pinscher lines gave it a history of its own as a close household dog.
VBO:0200893.shortDescription: Lively and self-assured, the Miniature Pinscher is quick to notice its surroundings yet even in familiar company.
VBO:0200893.historicalRoots: German small pinscher established before the twentieth century.

VBO:0200894.summary: Miniature Pinschers are lively, spirited and self-assured, yet tend to keep an even temperament. They were already kept in large numbers around the turn of the twentieth century; Germany’s 1925 stud book recorded at least 1,300 entries, a measure of how established this small companion breed had become.
VBO:0200894.shortDescription: A lively, self-assured small Pinscher with an even temperament and a long German breed history.
VBO:0200894.historicalRoots: German Miniature Pinscher, numerous by the early twentieth century.

VBO:0200895.summary: Often lively and self-assured, red Miniature Pinschers combine a spirited manner with an even temperament. They were already common in Germany around the turn of the twentieth century, with about 1,300 dogs entered in the 1925 studbook. Solid red and black-and-tan survived the selection from a broader range of earlier colours.
VBO:0200895.shortDescription: An often lively, self-assured German companion whose red variety shares the Miniature Pinscher’s spirited character.
VBO:0200895.historicalRoots: German Miniature Pinscher companion population, numerous by the turn of the twentieth century; selected solid red variety.

VBO:0200896.summary: Alert, intelligent and fearless, the Miniature Schnauzer tends to notice activity around a home and make its presence known. It grew from small rough-haired farm dogs of the Frankfurt region; the watchful temperament links that working ancestry to its long role as a close companion.
VBO:0200896.shortDescription: Alert and fearless, the Miniature Schnauzer notices activity around the home, echoing its rough-haired farm-dog roots.
VBO:0200896.historicalRoots: German small rough-haired pinscher and Schnauzer tradition.

VBO:0200897.summary: Alert and fearless, the black-and-silver Miniature Schnauzer carries a watchful, tenacious character. German farmers developed these small dogs to pursue rodents in houses and barns; the color now called black and silver was once described as black and tan. The breed also settled into a companion and watchdog role.
VBO:0200897.shortDescription: Alert and fearless, this black-and-silver Miniature Schnauzer carries a German farm-ratting past.
VBO:0200897.historicalRoots: Developed in Germany around the turn of the twentieth century; black-and-silver descended from an earlier black-and-tan color designation.

VBO:0200898.summary: Fearless and watchful, the pepper-and-salt Miniature Schnauzer brings a durable little dog's energy to its companion role. The breed emerged around Frankfurt from smaller rough-haired farm dogs, then earned its place as a sharp-eyed household watchdog; German farmers also bred Minis to pursue rats and other small pests indoors and around barns.
VBO:0200898.shortDescription: Fearless and watchful, this pepper-and-salt Miniature Schnauzer recalls the breed's farm-ratting roots.
VBO:0200898.historicalRoots: German breed shaped near Frankfurt around 1900 from smaller rough-haired dogs; pepper-and-salt is an FCI-recognized coat variety.

VBO:0200899.summary: Miniature Schnauzers bring fearless alertness and stamina to the watchful companion role. Around 1900 in the Frankfurt area, breeders shaped rough-haired small pinschers into a miniature counterpart of the Schnauzer, seeking the larger breed’s characteristic qualities in a smaller dog.
VBO:0200899.shortDescription: Fearless and alert, this Miniature Schnauzer traces its roots to small rough-haired dogs around Frankfurt.

VBO:0200900.summary: Miniature Schnauzers tend to be alert, fearless and enduring companions. Early breeders around Frankfurt had to work through dogs with varied sizes, shapes and coat textures to establish a small dog with the distinctive qualities of the larger Schnauzer.
VBO:0200900.shortDescription: Alert and enduring, this Miniature Schnauzer brings a watchful temperament to companion life.

VBO:0200901.summary: Miniature Schnoodle is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200902.summary: Mixed Breed is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200903.summary: Molossus is a historical dog breed or type associated with Epirus.

VBO:0200904.summary: In Greece’s breed ideal, the contemporary Molossus of Epirus is devoted to its flock and owner and friendly with familiar people. Its work is guarding livestock in Epirus and nearby mountain areas, protecting flocks against large predators when needed.
VBO:0200904.shortDescription: A contemporary Greek livestock guardian, described as devoted to its flock and owner and friendly with familiar people.

VBO:0200906.summary: Balanced and closely attached to its handler, the Montenegrin Mountain Hound brings steady persistence to a scent trail. It belongs to the Balkan tradition of hunting through rugged country, following quarry with a dependable working style.
VBO:0200906.shortDescription: Balanced and attached to its handler, this Montenegrin hound follows scent steadily through rugged Balkan country.

VBO:0200907.summary: Playful, sociable individuals of this Maltese–Yorkshire Terrier cross have trained for therapy work. In South Africa, Dr Suné Scholtz’s dog Morkie joined children’s play-therapy sessions, responding to hand signals and voice commands. In Indiana, Rocky completed a Love on a Leash evaluation and ten supervised visits, with his handler describing a friendly dog comfortable with adults and children.
VBO:0200907.shortDescription: Selected Maltese–Yorkshire Terrier crosses have trained as therapy dogs for children’s sessions and library visits.
VBO:0200907.historicalRoots: Named Maltese–Yorkshire Terrier cross with documented individually trained child play-therapy and library-visiting dogs.

VBO:0200909.summary: Moscow Toy, Long-Haired Terrier is a variety of Russian Toy.

VBO:0200910.summary: Moscow Toy, Short-Haired Terrier is a variety of Russian Toy.

VBO:0200911.summary: Moscow Vodolaz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200912.summary: Self-confident and devoted to its household, the Moscow Watchdog combines a pronounced guarding instinct with a balanced, responsive manner. Its working ideal pairs independence with close cooperation with people. Developed at Moscow’s Red Star military breeding kennel in the 1950s, it drew on Caucasian Shepherd, Saint Bernard and Russian piebald hound ancestry.
VBO:0200912.shortDescription: A self-confident, devoted Moscow guardian, bred for a balanced manner and a strong instinct to watch over its household.

VBO:0200913.summary: Moscow Water Dog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Russia.

VBO:0200914.summary: Keen to work with its handler, the Mountain Cur brings strong treeing instincts and persistence to a hunt. It often follows a trail with its head raised, circling an older scent until a fresher trail appears; its voice may range from silent to freely barking. Rural American breeders preserved it for squirrel, raccoon and larger game.
VBO:0200914.shortDescription: A persistent tree dog that tends to hunt with its head raised, circling older scent to find a fresher trail.

VBO:0200915.summary: Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200916.summary: Extremely alert, the Mountain Feist hunts with sight, hearing and scent while staying almost silent on a trail. This agile small tree dog was shaped in the rural American South for squirrels, other small game and vermin control. Generations of selection have focused on practical performance, including quick movement over rough terrain.
VBO:0200916.shortDescription: An extremely alert southern American tree dog, tracking quietly with sight, hearing and scent before locating small game.

VBO:0200917.summary: Mountain Stephens Stock Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200918.summary: Mountain View Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200919.summary: Mucuchies are known in Venezuela for loyalty, intelligence and a protective character, with their story closely tied to the Andean town that gave them their name. One dog, Nevado, holds a special place in national memory as Simón Bolívar’s companion. Cultural accounts of Nevado have helped make the breed a living symbol of Venezuelan history.
VBO:0200919.shortDescription: Known for loyalty and a protective nature, the Mucuchies also carries the Venezuelan memory of Bolívar’s companion Nevado.
VBO:0200919.historicalRoots: Venezuelan Andean farm and livestock-guardian dog.

VBO:0200920.summary: The Mudhol Hound is valued for speed and stamina in open-country pursuit across northern Karnataka and the western Deccan. Regional families have used it for hunting, guarding and companionship, linking a keen chase response with watch duties near home. Its working history is especially associated with villages around Bagalkot.
VBO:0200920.shortDescription: Valued for speed and stamina, the Mudhol Hound pursued game across the Deccan and kept watch near village homes.
VBO:0200920.historicalRoots: Karnataka sighthound of the western Deccan.

VBO:0200921.summary: The Mudi is often quick to learn, eager to work and courageous around difficult livestock. This Hungarian herder also took part in wild-boar drives and watched property, so its lively attention was useful across several rural jobs; it can switch from close stock control to sounding an alarm.
VBO:0200921.shortDescription: Quick to learn and courageous with livestock, the Mudi can switch from close herding to watching property.
VBO:0200921.historicalRoots: Hungarian herding dog from local and prick-eared German stock.

VBO:0200922.summary: Lively, alert and adaptable in its breed standard, the ash-colored Mudi shares the working character of the other colors. Hungarian shepherds use Mudis with large and difficult livestock, and the standard also records their use in wild-boar drives. Their independently turning ears give the watchful farm dog a distinctive expression.
VBO:0200922.shortDescription: An ash-colored Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively, alert character and livestock-working tradition.

VBO:0200923.summary: Watchful and lively, Mudi tend to be keen to work, adaptable and ready to learn. These Hungarian herders have handled large, difficult livestock and also served as watch and alarm dogs. The breed took shape in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries from Hungarian herding stock, probably crossed with prick-eared German herders.
VBO:0200923.shortDescription: A lively, watchful Hungarian herder, quick to learn and keen to work; this variety has a black coat.

VBO:0200924.summary: Lively, alert and keen to work in its breed standard, the Mudi is a Hungarian herder used with large and difficult livestock. The same standard describes courage, watchfulness and adaptability, and records work in wild-boar drives. Blue-merle denotes a coat pattern; these working tendencies belong to the breed rather than its color.
VBO:0200924.shortDescription: A lively, alert Hungarian herder in the standard; blue-merle is a coat pattern, with the same working character.

VBO:0200925.summary: Lively and watchful in the breed standard, Mudis are keen workers with a capacity for learning. Hungarian shepherds use them to herd large, difficult livestock, drawing on the breed’s courageous disposition. Their ears can turn independently. Brown is a coat form of this same working breed, with no separate character assigned to its color.
VBO:0200925.shortDescription: A brown-coated Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively, watchful character and work with difficult livestock.

VBO:0200926.summary: Keen to learn and ready for work in its breed standard, the fawn Mudi shares the breed’s lively, courageous character. Hungarian shepherds use Mudis to move large and difficult livestock; watch and alarm work is also documented. Their ears can turn independently, an expressive detail of an alert herding dog.
VBO:0200926.shortDescription: A fawn Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively character, readiness to learn and livestock-working tradition.

VBO:0200927.summary: Alert, lively and watchful in its breed standard, the white Mudi shares its working character with the other coat forms. This Hungarian herder is used with large and difficult livestock and in wild-boar drives. Its ears can turn independently, a distinctive expression of the responsive farm dog described by the standard.
VBO:0200927.shortDescription: A white-coated Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively, watchful character and livestock-working tradition.

VBO:0200928.summary: Munsterlander Pointer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200930.summary: Steady and loyal, the Neapolitan Mastiff remains alert to activity around the home despite its often quiet manner. Its southern Italian history centers on property guarding around Naples and Mount Vesuvius. Ancient Roman mastiff associations add depth, but its long local guardian role is the clearest thread in the breed’s story.
VBO:0200930.shortDescription: Steady and loyal, the Neapolitan Mastiff keeps a quiet watch around homes, reflecting southern Italian guarding work.

VBO:0200931.summary: Nebolish Mastiff is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200932.summary: The Nederlandse Kooikerhondje tends to be alert and energetic, persistent at work without being needlessly noisy. At a Dutch duck decoy it moves between reed screens and waves its tail to draw curious ducks into a trap; it does not retrieve them. It also historically hunted vermin, giving this small working spaniel two distinctive jobs.
VBO:0200932.shortDescription: Alert but not needlessly noisy, the Kooikerhondje lures ducks through reed screens by flashing its tail; it does not retrieve them.
VBO:0200932.historicalRoots: Dutch duck-decoy worker revived in the 1940s.

VBO:0200933.summary: Nenets Herding Laikas tend to be lively and friendly, eager to learn yet able to decide for themselves. Their strong inborn herding instinct developed around moving reindeer in Russia’s far north, where a close bond with people was also part of the breed’s working life.
VBO:0200933.shortDescription: Lively and independent-minded, this far-northern Russian herder works closely with people and reindeer.
VBO:0200933.historicalRoots: Nenets reindeer-herding dog of the Russian far north.

VBO:0200934.summary: New Guinea Singing Dogs are remarkable communicators, producing wavering, musical howls. Their close wild relatives in the New Guinea highlands are shy and elusive, making field observation difficult. A 2020 genetic study linked those highland dogs with the captive singing-dog population, opening a new chapter in the conservation of this unusual canine lineage.
VBO:0200934.shortDescription: Known for wavering, musical howls, the New Guinea Singing Dog has elusive highland relatives whose habits remain hard to observe.
VBO:0200934.historicalRoots: New Guinea free-ranging dog lineage represented by both wild-associated and captive populations.

VBO:0200935.summary: The New Zealand Heading Dog controls sheep with movement and a fixed gaze, often circling wide before bringing a flock toward its handler. Unlike the barking Huntaway, it is selected to work quietly; farmers value that close, precise control for yard work such as separating sheep from a mob.
VBO:0200935.shortDescription: Working quietly, the New Zealand Heading Dog circles wide and controls sheep with movement and a fixed gaze.
VBO:0200935.historicalRoots: New Zealand sheep-heading dog developed from Border Collies.

VBO:0200937.summary: New Zealand Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200938.summary: Newfoundlands are known for a gentle, composed disposition, with a joyful side alongside their calmness. Their working history in Canada joins two demanding jobs: hauling heavy loads on land and helping people in the water, including rescue work. The breed’s reputation rests as much on that steady character and willingness to work as on its swimming ability.
VBO:0200938.shortDescription: Gentle and composed with a joyful side, the Newfoundland once hauled loads on land and helped people in water.
VBO:0200938.historicalRoots: Canadian working water dog associated with Newfoundland fisheries and rescue work.

registryGroups.label: Group 2 · Pinscher and Schnauzer - Molossoid and Swiss Mountain and Cattledogs

VBO:0200939.summary: Gentle and serene, Newfoundlands are also described as dignified and joyful. The black variety shares the breed’s working history on Newfoundland’s coast, pulling heavy loads on land and serving as a water dog. Its swimming is aided by a strong tail that acts as a rudder.
VBO:0200939.shortDescription: A gentle, dignified black water dog with a working history of swimming and hauling heavy loads on land.

VBO:0200940.summary: Brown Newfoundlands share the breed’s notable gentleness and serenity, along with a joyful, dignified character. On the island of Newfoundland, dogs of this type hauled heavy loads on land and worked in cold water; their strength and composure also made them lifeguards for people facing rough seas.
VBO:0200940.shortDescription: A gentle, serene brown Newfoundland rooted in heavy hauling and cold-water rescue work.
VBO:0200940.historicalRoots: Island of Newfoundland working water dog and heavy-load hauler.

VBO:0200941.summary: Usually gentle and composed, yet capable of playfulness, the Landseer Newfoundland belongs to a long tradition of work around boats and water. Newfoundlands hauled loads and served aboard ships; their swimming strength made them valuable for water rescues. The Landseer name remembers Sir Edwin Landseer’s paintings, which helped popularize white-and-black Newfoundlands in the nineteenth century.
VBO:0200941.shortDescription: A usually gentle, composed Newfoundland variety whose Landseer name recalls nineteenth-century paintings.
VBO:0200941.historicalRoots: White-and-black Newfoundland variety named for Sir Edwin Landseer; Canadian draft and ship-dog tradition.

VBO:0200942.summary: Griffon Nivernais bring courage and initiative to difficult scent trails, with a marked taste for rough ground and thickets. Their working style favors staying power over speed, and they can be independent or obstinate. Recreated in the Nivernais region during the late nineteenth century, they remain associated chiefly with wild-boar hunting in small packs or alone.
VBO:0200942.shortDescription: A courageous, independent French griffon that persists through rough ground and thickets on scent trails.
VBO:0200942.historicalRoots: Recreated in the Nivernais region in the late 19th and early 20th centuries with Vendéen, Foxhound and Otterhound contributions.

VBO:0200944.summary: Norfolk Spaniel is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200945.summary: Boldly curious yet companionable, the Norfolk Terrier brings a small hunter’s resolve to new activity. East Anglian farm dogs needed courage for vermin work in tight places; an old saying called the breed “a demon for its size.” Its shared farm history with the Norwich Terrier still explains its busy, persistent character.
VBO:0200945.shortDescription: Boldly curious and companionable, the Norfolk Terrier keeps the persistence of an East Anglian farm vermin hunter.
VBO:0200945.historicalRoots: East Anglian farm and vermin terrier.

VBO:0200946.summary: Norman Artesien Bassets are outgoing, affectionate hounds whose patient trail work has a melodious soundtrack. They follow a line steadily rather than quickly, hunting alone or in a pack. Their short legs let them enter dense vegetation that larger hounds cannot reach, especially in pursuit of rabbits, their traditional favorite quarry.
VBO:0200946.shortDescription: An affectionate, outgoing French basset that follows rabbit trails patiently, giving a melodious voice.
VBO:0200946.historicalRoots: Controlled French basset breeding from the 1870s; Basset Artésien Normand name adopted in 1924.

VBO:0200947.summary: Norman Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200948.summary: The Norrbottenspets is often lively, alert and quick to use its voice when something catches its attention. This bold but kindly northern hunter is especially associated with barking at forest birds in trees. The breed survived on remote Swedish homesteads after it had been declared extinct.
VBO:0200948.shortDescription: Lively and vocal, the Norrbottenspets is known for barking at forest birds in trees during a hunt.
VBO:0200948.historicalRoots: Northern Swedish hunting spitz, preserved on Norrbotten homesteads.

VBO:0200950.summary: North Country Beagle is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200951.summary: Northeasterly Hauling Laika is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200952.summary: Northern Inuit Dogs tend to be friendly, placid and outgoing, with an inquisitive streak that rewards varied training. Developed in Britain from northern breeds and German Shepherds beginning in the 1980s, they were shaped for a wolf-like outline while remaining domestic companions.
VBO:0200952.shortDescription: A friendly, inquisitive British-developed dog with a northern outline and a need for varied training.
VBO:0200952.historicalRoots: British Northern Inuit breeding program begun in the 1980s.

VBO:0200953.summary: The Norwegian Buhund tends to be courageous and energetic but also friendly, a combination suited to daily work alongside people. It was a versatile farmstead dog, helping herd livestock and keeping watch around Norwegian holdings. The name itself points to the farmstead, and old accounts place buhund-type dogs in Norway far back toward the Viking Age.
VBO:0200953.shortDescription: Courageous, energetic, and friendly, the Norwegian Buhund helped herd livestock and watch over farmsteads.
VBO:0200953.historicalRoots: Norwegian farm, herding and watch dog with old spitz roots.

VBO:0200954.summary: Norwegian Dunker Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200955.summary: The Norwegian Elkhound brings courage, stamina and quick judgment to moose hunting. It can track through rough northern country, then bark, dodge and circle to hold a much larger animal until a hunter arrives; that mix of persistence and agility is the skill behind its name.
VBO:0200955.shortDescription: Courageous and agile, the Norwegian Elkhound can bark, dodge, and circle moose until a hunter reaches it.

VBO:0200956.summary: Brave and energetic on a hunt, the Black Norwegian Elkhound works close to its handler and is valued for quiet cooperation. In Norway it tracks elk and deer on a lead, staying calm near game so the hunter can approach; away from work, the breed is known for a devoted bond with its family.
VBO:0200956.shortDescription: Brave yet quietly cooperative, the Black Norwegian Elkhound tracks elk and deer on a lead close to its handler.
VBO:0200956.historicalRoots: Norwegian black elkhound specialized for leashed big-game tracking.

VBO:0200957.summary: Norwegian Elkhound Grey is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200962.summary: Busy and fearless, Norwich Terriers also tend to be companionable with familiar people. They emerged from East Anglian farm dogs that hunted vermin wherever a small, tenacious worker could fit. That tireless interest in their surroundings outlasted the old farm setting and remains central to the breed’s character.
VBO:0200962.shortDescription: Busy, fearless, and companionable, the Norwich Terrier retains a keen interest in its surroundings from farm vermin work.
VBO:0200962.historicalRoots: East Anglian farm and vermin terrier.

VBO:0200964.summary: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever tends to be quick to fetch, intelligent and trainable, with the endurance to swim for game. It plays an unusual two-part hunting role: its playful movement near shore draws waterfowl closer, and then it retrieves them from land or water.
VBO:0200964.shortDescription: Playful movement near shore draws ducks closer; then this eager retriever fetches them from land or water.
VBO:0200964.historicalRoots: Nova Scotian waterfowl tolling and retrieving dog of the nineteenth century.

VBO:0200965.summary: Old Croatian Sighthound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200967.summary: Old English Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200969.summary: Steady, biddable, and bold, the Old English Sheepdog was a country worker before it became a familiar companion. Cooperation with people served sheep work through changing weather and long days.
VBO:0200969.shortDescription: Steady and biddable, the Old English Sheepdog cooperated with people through long days of country sheep work.
VBO:0200969.historicalRoots: British country sheepdog with mixed historical roots.

VBO:0200970.summary: Old English Terrier is a historical dog breed or type associated with England and United Kingdom.

VBO:0200971.summary: Adaptability and useful work lie at the heart of the Old Farm Collie tradition. Scottish farm dogs helped herd, guard and drive sheep; modern preservation groups seek to keep that versatility alongside companionship. Their revival followed a twentieth-century decline in these farm collies. As a landrace, the type allows variation while favoring sound, moderate dogs and working ability over show-ring exaggeration.
VBO:0200971.shortDescription: A versatile farm-collie tradition, revived to preserve useful work and companionship within a varied landrace.
VBO:0200971.historicalRoots: Scottish farm-collie landrace; modern preservation revival after twentieth-century decline.

VBO:0200972.summary: Old Spanish Pointer is a historical dog breed or type associated with Spain.

VBO:0200973.summary: Old Time Farm Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200974.summary: Old Welsh Grey Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Wales.

VBO:0200975.summary: Olde Boston Bulldogge is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200976.summary: Olde English Bulldogges are confident and friendly dogs with an alert, animated manner. A breeding project begun in 1971 set out to restore the agility and working ability of a Regency-period bulldog; the UKC describes today’s breed first as a companion while retaining scope for varied work.
VBO:0200976.shortDescription: Confident and friendly, this animated bulldog arose from a 1971 project to restore working ability.
VBO:0200976.historicalRoots: Modern American reconstruction begun in 1971 to evoke a functional Regency-era bulldog.

VBO:0200977.summary: Olde Victorian Bulldogge is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200978.summary: Ori-Pei was developed by Aaron Silver in North America during the 1970s as a smaller companion with Shar-Pei and Pug ancestry. The project continued across several generations, so the name covers descendants of that original pairing rather than one fixed first-generation mix.
VBO:0200978.shortDescription: Developed in North America in the 1970s, this Shar-Pei–Pug companion cross continued through several generations.
VBO:0200978.historicalRoots: North American Shar-Pei/Pug breeding project begun by Aaron Silver in the1970s.

VBO:0200979.summary: Original English Bulldogge is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200980.summary: The Otterhound is often amiable and even-tempered away from the demanding scent work for which it was bred. It followed scent over both bank and water, announcing a promising trail with its deep bay. Houndsmen distinguished a land “drag” from a waterborne “wash,” and the breed was built to keep going through either.
VBO:0200980.shortDescription: Amiable off duty, the Otterhound follows scent over bank and water, giving a deep bay when a trail turns promising.
VBO:0200980.historicalRoots: British otter-trailing scent hound, a former hunting role.

VBO:0200981.summary: Ovtcharka is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200982.summary: Calm, biddable and sociable, the Pachon Navarro has a cooperative working style. This Spanish pointing dog searches at a vigorous trot close to the hunter, working in tandem. Its revival drew on old Spanish pointing-dog stock.
VBO:0200982.shortDescription: A calm, sociable Spanish pointing dog that hunts at a vigorous trot close to its handler.

VBO:0200983.summary: Paisley Terrier is a dog breed or regional type associated with Scotland.

VBO:0200984.summary: Responsive to its owner and reserved with strangers, the Pampas Deerhound is the Brazilian Veadeiro Pampeano. It can track and pursue furred game beyond its handler’s sight, working alone or with other dogs; its standard calls for a calm manner within the hunting group. The breed is particularly associated with Rio Grande do Sul.
VBO:0200984.shortDescription: A Brazilian hunting dog, responsive to its owner and reserved with strangers, working alone or in a calm group.

VBO:0200985.summary: Papillon is a variety of Continental Toy Spaniel.

VBO:0200987.summary: Parson Russell Terriers are often confident, energetic and friendly, with the boldness of a dog bred to work below ground. Their fox-working history explains the breed’s agile, persistent style. The name honors the Reverend John Russell, whose Victorian hunting terriers shaped the strain later recognized as a separate breed.
VBO:0200987.shortDescription: Confident and energetic, the Parson Russell Terrier brings fox-working boldness to agile pursuit below ground.
VBO:0200987.historicalRoots: British fox-working terrier associated with Reverend John Russell

VBO:0200988.summary: Pastore della Lessinia e del Lagorai dogs are attentive, balanced herders that move livestock across long, uneven alpine routes. The Italian standard describes an especially strong sense of spatial orientation and a close working bond with people. Transhumant flocks shaped this breed in the mountains and foothills of northeastern Italy.
VBO:0200988.shortDescription: An attentive alpine herder with endurance and a strong sense of direction on long drives.
VBO:0200988.historicalRoots: Northeastern Italian mountain and prealpine transhumant livestock driving.

VBO:0200989.summary: Patagonian Sheepdogs were shaped by practical flock work in southern Chile after European sheepdogs reached the region. They still help manage sheep, and sometimes cattle, on widely separated farms; generations of selection and geographic isolation gave this regional working population a history distinct from its imported ancestors.
VBO:0200989.shortDescription: Patagonian Sheepdogs still manage sheep and sometimes cattle on distant Chilean farms, shaped by generations of local work.

VBO:0200990.summary: Patterdale Terriers are bold, active dogs with a strong prey drive and a marked willingness to work with their people. Developed among northern England's fell terriers, they followed quarry into tight burrows and held it at bay; their work was tied to controlling vermin around sheep country.
VBO:0200990.shortDescription: Bold and keen to work, this northern English earth terrier follows quarry into tight burrows.
VBO:0200990.historicalRoots: Northern English Fell Terrier developed for underground vermin work in sheep country.

VBO:0200991.summary: Fond of sunbathing and watching passers-by from a windowsill, sixteen-month-old Patterjack Kiba offers a keeper’s account of this Patterdale Terrier–Jack Russell Terrier cross. She hid chews in the laundry and behind the television, and spent time sniffing through woodland undergrowth.
VBO:0200991.shortDescription: A Patterdale–Jack Russell cross; Kiba’s keeper described sunbathing, windowsill watching and hiding chews around the home.

VBO:0200992.summary: Enthusiastic about digging in the sand, Tilly the Patterpoo joined Neil Morris and his wife on coastal walks on the Isle of Man. In his 2020 account, Morris described a dog who avoided the noisy sea but loved splashing in the calm, shallow pools left by the tide. Patterpoo is a name for a Patterdale Terrier–Poodle cross.
VBO:0200992.shortDescription: A Patterdale–Poodle cross; Neil Morris’s Tilly enjoyed beach digging and calm tidal pools while avoiding the noisy sea.

VBO:0200993.summary: Affectionate close company and toy play recur in adult rescue accounts of the Pekepoo, a Pekingese–Poodle cross. Willow greets familiar people with stuffed animals, chases squirrels and barks at deliveries. Morrie enjoys walks, toys and couch time beside his person. Both accounts also describe anxiety and strong reactions around particular people, dogs or possessions.
VBO:0200993.shortDescription: A Pekingese–Poodle cross whose adult rescue accounts describe close company, toy play and watchful reactions.

VBO:0200994.summary: Fearless and loyal to familiar people, the Pekingese has a distinctly self-possessed manner. It was bred for companionship in China and tends to meet strangers with dignified reserve. That combination of closeness and independence gives the small dog a character that can feel larger than its size.
VBO:0200994.shortDescription: Fearless and loyal with familiar people, the Pekingese combines close companionship with dignified reserve toward strangers.

VBO:0200995.summary: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi tends to be bold, outgoing and friendly, with stamina to keep moving as livestock changes direction. It was bred to work sheep and cattle, staying mobile and alert around animals much larger than itself. The farm role rewarded initiative as well as a close response to its handler.
VBO:0200995.shortDescription: Bold and outgoing, the Pembroke Welsh Corgi keeps moving around larger livestock while watching its handler.
VBO:0200995.historicalRoots: Welsh cattle herder with a compact low build.

VBO:0200996.summary: Pencil-Tail Feist is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200997.summary: Perdiguero de Burgos dogs are calm, docile hunters with a strong nose and a firm, persistent way of following a trail. The Spanish pointer is valued for pointing and retrieving feathered and small game across difficult ground. Though usually trained for smaller quarry, the breed also has a history of boldly tackling larger game.
VBO:0200997.shortDescription: Calm and persistent, this Burgos pointer uses a keen nose to track, point and retrieve across rough ground.

VBO:0201003.summary: Perro Majoreros tend to be loyal and strongly territorial, warm with familiar people but wary of strangers. On Fuerteventura they directed livestock without harming it and guarded property; their sure-footed movement over rough lava ground was part of that working life.
VBO:0201003.shortDescription: Loyal to familiar people and wary of strangers, this Fuerteventura worker herded stock and watched property.
VBO:0201003.historicalRoots: Fuerteventura livestock driving and property guarding on rough volcanic terrain.

VBO:0201004.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dogs tend to be affectionate with their own people and more cautious around strangers, combining close companionship with an alert watchdog instinct. Their cultural history reaches far beyond the modern breed: depictions appear in the ceramics of several pre-Inca societies, including the Moche and Chancay.
VBO:0201004.shortDescription: Affectionate with familiar people but cautious with strangers, this Peruvian dog combines companionship with alert watchfulness.
VBO:0201004.interestingFact: Viringo is another name for the Peruvian Hairless Dog.
VBO:0201004.historicalRoots: Ancient Peruvian hairless-dog tradition documented in pre-Columbian art.

VBO:0201005.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dogs are lively, alert companions, affectionate with familiar people and sometimes wary of strangers. Their watchful role has endured alongside a much older cultural presence: the breed appears in ceramics from several pre-Inca societies. Official recognition in 1985 gave this native breed a modern standard.
VBO:0201005.shortDescription: A lively, affectionate Peruvian companion with watchful instincts and pre-Inca roots.
VBO:0201005.historicalRoots: Pre-Inca Peruvian ceramics, followed by modern recognition of the native breed in 1985.

VBO:0201006.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dogs tend to be lively and alert yet affectionate with those close to them, and may hold back around strangers. Their role as watchful companions is documented in the breed standard. Peruvian ceramics from several pre-Inca cultures show the hairless dog, a record much older than its official 1985 recognition.
VBO:0201006.shortDescription: An alert, affectionate Peruvian companion that may be reserved with unfamiliar people.
VBO:0201006.historicalRoots: Pre-Inca Peruvian cultural record; modern FCI recognition of the native breed in 1985.

VBO:0201007.summary: Affectionate with familiar people but sometimes reserved with strangers, the miniature Peruvian Hairless Dog is described as lively and alert. Its watchfulness sits alongside a long history as a companion. Known in Peru as the viringo, hairless dogs appear on pre-Inca pottery, including pieces from the Mochica and Chancay cultures. This is the smallest of the breed’s three size varieties.
VBO:0201007.shortDescription: An alert, affectionate companion with familiar people, the smallest viringo carries a history seen in pre-Inca pottery.
VBO:0201007.historicalRoots: Peru is the primary standard’s origin. A dry coastal path is art direction, not a claimed historical subregion or a pottery reconstruction.

VBO:0201009.summary: Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201010.summary: Petit Bleu de Gascogne hounds are calm and affectionate, yet intent when working a scent. They cooperate well in a pack and are known for a fine nose and a beautiful voice; hare is a favored quarry, though the standard also records big-game work. The breed came from a deliberate reduction in size of the Grand Bleu de Gascogne, shaped by hunting needs in France.
VBO:0201010.shortDescription: Calm and affectionate, this French pack hound follows hare with a fine nose and distinctive voice.
VBO:0201010.historicalRoots: French Gascony scent hound selected in a smaller size

VBO:0201011.summary: Petit Brabançons tend to be proud, alert little companions, watchful and strongly attached to familiar people. They share the Brussels stable-dog ancestry of the rough-coated Griffons, where guarding carriages and hunting rodents were everyday tasks. Nineteenth-century Pug and toy-spaniel crosses helped shape the smooth-coated type.
VBO:0201011.shortDescription: A proud, alert Belgian companion, watchful and devoted, with roots in Brussels carriage and stable work.
