They were bred when larger Swiss Hounds were judged too fast for enclosed hunting grounds, and the smaller dogs kept a keen nose for searching difficult terrain and following wounded game.
VBO:0201252.shortDescription: A friendly, determined Swiss trail hound bred for smaller hunting grounds and a singing voice.
VBO:0201252.historicalRoots: Swiss short-legged hound selected for enclosed hunting grounds around the turn of the twentieth century.

VBO:0201253.summary: Friendly and determined on a scent trail, the Small Jura Hound shares the Swiss Short-Legged Hound’s hunting character. It follows game independently and gives tongue with a melodious cry, including on difficult ground. Smaller hounds were developed for enclosed Swiss hunting grounds around 1900; Jura denotes the black-and-tan color variety.
VBO:0201253.shortDescription: A black-and-tan Swiss hound variety, sharing the breed’s friendly character, independent scent work and melodious cry.

VBO:0201254.summary: Friendly and tireless on the trail in its standard, the Small Lucerne Hound shares the Swiss Short-Legged Hound’s hunting character. It searches independently and announces pursuit with a melodious cry; tracking wounded game is another documented role. Lucerne denotes the blue-speckled, black-mantled color variety within the shared modern breed.
VBO:0201254.shortDescription: A blue-speckled Swiss hound variety, sharing the breed’s friendly character, independent hunting and melodious cry.

VBO:0201255.summary: Friendly and steady on a trail in its standard, the Small Schwyz Hound shares the Swiss Short-Legged Hound’s hunting character. It searches and drives game with a melodious cry, even on difficult terrain, and is also used to track wounded game. Schwyz identifies the white-and-orange color variety within the modern shared breed.
VBO:0201255.shortDescription: A white-and-orange Swiss hound variety, sharing the breed’s friendly character, steady scent work and melodious cry.

VBO:0201256.summary: Boisterous and outgoing, Tasmanian Smithfields can retain the independent approach of a farm worker. Breeder Matthew Larner describes dogs that start training later and work more naturally than more controllable herding dogs. Farmers have shaped this variable working type for moving cattle and sheep, while keeping it as a companion too.
VBO:0201256.shortDescription: An outgoing Tasmanian working type, shaped by farmers for cattle and sheep and described as a natural worker.

VBO:0201257.summary: Smooth Beagle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201258.summary: Smooth Fox Terriers are lively, sociable and quick to meet a new challenge. Britain’s foxhunts shaped a dog ready to pursue foxes, and the old working brief also included rats and rabbits. Their bright, expectant manner hints at a terrier that was bred to move fast and keep its attention on the task.
VBO:0201258.shortDescription: Lively and sociable, the Smooth Fox Terrier reacts quickly to a challenge, reflecting fox, rat, and rabbit work.
VBO:0201258.historicalRoots: British foxhunting terrier standardized by the late 19th century.

VBO:0201260.summary: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier is a variety of Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201261.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, English American Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201262.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, Heavy Irish Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201263.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, Traditional Irish Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201264.summary: South Russian Shepherd Dogs tend to be self-confident and independent, strongly devoted to their people but reserved with strangers. Their long shaggy coat can hide an agile worker: they guarded cattle and property across open southern steppe country. The breed took its modern name and formal shape in the early twentieth century after earlier bearded herding dogs mixed with local stock.
VBO:0201264.shortDescription: Self-confident and devoted to its people, this shaggy steppe guardian remains reserved with strangers.
VBO:0201264.historicalRoots: Southern Russian steppe herding and guardian breed, standardized in the early twentieth century.

VBO:0201265.summary: South Russian Steppe Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201267.summary: Southern Blackmouth Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201268.summary: Southern Bloodhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201270.summary: Southern Hound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201271.summary: Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201275.summary: Spanish Hounds are affectionate and calm off the hunt, yet notably brave when following larger game. Hunters listen to changes in the hound's voice to tell whether it has found an old line, a fresh one or the end of a chase. The Sabueso also has a long reputation for hare work, recorded in Spanish hunting writing since the late Middle Ages.
VBO:0201275.shortDescription: Calm and affectionate off the hunt, this Spanish hound changes its voice as a scent trail develops.
VBO:0201275.historicalRoots: Sabueso Español documented in late-medieval Spanish hunting texts; specialist in hare and blood tracking.

VBO:0201276.summary: Spanish Hound, Large is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201277.summary: Spanish Hound, Small is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201278.summary: The Spanish Mastiff tends to pair affection toward familiar people with resolve when stock or property is threatened. It traveled with Merino flocks on seasonal routes, staying close enough to defend animals from wolves in changing pastures. Its story is inseparable from Spain’s old transhumant sheep culture and the medieval Mesta.
VBO:0201278.shortDescription: Affectionate with familiar people yet resolute on guard, the Spanish Mastiff defended Merino flocks on seasonal routes.
VBO:0201278.historicalRoots: Spanish transhumant flock guardian, especially with Merino sheep.

VBO:0201280.summary: Spanish Water Dogs tend to be lively, watchful and quick to grasp a task, with a strong willingness to work alongside people. Their traditional jobs ranged across herding, hunting and assisting fishermen. Readiness to learn and adapt to changing conditions was useful across that varied working life.
VBO:0201280.shortDescription: Lively and watchful, the Spanish Water Dog learned varied work beside people, from herding to fishing and hunting.
VBO:0201280.historicalRoots: Spanish multipurpose working dog used for herding and water-related tasks.

registryGroups.label: Group 8 · Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs

VBO:0201282.summary: Spitz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201284.summary: Determined and alert, the Sporting Lucas Terrier tends to bring a keen, independent approach to hunting while remaining responsive to direction. Its working role includes pushing game out of thick cover and pursuing ground vermin above and below ground. British breeders maintain this compact terrier primarily for that work.
VBO:0201284.shortDescription: A determined working terrier, keen to search thick cover and tackle ground vermin while responding to direction.

VBO:0201285.summary: Lively and affectionate in one rescue’s firsthand observations, the Springador is a Labrador–Springer Spaniel cross with documented working roles. Molly, an adult in foster care, is described as clever and communicative, with a chase instinct and a need for close company. Kenya Customs’ Cooper belongs to a trained patrol team detecting narcotics and explosives across borders.
VBO:0201285.shortDescription: A Labrador–Springer Spaniel cross, seen in customs scent work and described in rescue care as lively and affectionate.

VBO:0201286.summary: Climbing is a memorable habit in Manorroy’s account of Martha, a Springbatt whose litter sister Beryl is described as especially cuddly. This Springer Spaniel–Basset cross appears in the kennel’s successive generations, which it traces back to breeding begun in 2003. A 2018 owner account contrasts Honey’s long walks with Clyde’s toy-taking and frequent pauses on walks.
VBO:0201286.shortDescription: A Springer Spaniel–Basset cross; Honey’s owner described long walks, while Clyde took toys and paused during walks.

VBO:0201287.summary: Springer Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201288.summary: Affectionate with rescue volunteers from her arrival, Springerdoodle Lacy enjoyed rolling over for belly rubs and spending time on laps. Phoenix Animal Rescue described her greeting visitors and dogs at a busy adoption event. Its account identified her as five years old and said her breeder had surrendered her when she was no longer wanted.
VBO:0201288.shortDescription: Phoenix Animal Rescue described Springerdoodle Lacy enjoying laps and belly rubs, and greeting visitors at an adoption event.

VBO:0201289.summary: Companionship and water are favorites of Harry, a ten-year-old Sprocker whom Malcata Animal Association described enjoying walks, swims and sofa evenings. This Springer–Cocker Spaniel cross appears in Liza Leonard’s firsthand account of Patch and Rufus: Patch approached for attention, while Rufus was initially shy; both liked balls and running.
VBO:0201289.shortDescription: Malcata described Harry as a Sprocker who loved water, walks and sofa company; Patch and Rufus enjoyed balls and running.

VBO:0201290.summary: Playing with tennis balls and enjoying the outdoors are part of Lenny’s keeper account, which calls this Sprockerpoo an energetic mix. Dexter’s community profile instead lists barking at intruders and sleeping among his hobbies, with an indiscriminate interest in human food. The name is used here for a Sprocker Spaniel–Poodle cross; another owner pictured their dog sunbathing.
VBO:0201290.shortDescription: A Sprocker Spaniel–Poodle cross; Lenny’s keeper described an energetic dog who loved tennis balls and nature.

VBO:0201292.summary: Calm and cheerful in her foster home, thirteen-year-old Bella illustrates one Oldies Club account of a Sprollie. She settled within a day after a sudden move from her previous home and liked resting beside her carer’s desk. Walks, garden pottering and staying close to people were favorite parts of her routine. The rescue described her as a Spaniel–Collie cross.
VBO:0201292.shortDescription: Bella’s foster carers described a calm, cheerful thirteen-year-old Sprollie who enjoyed walks and stayed close to people.

VBO:0201293.summary: Stabijhouns often combine affection with an independent streak; at home they can be quiet and watchful, while unfamiliar people may meet a reserved first response. Their Frisian farm history is unusually varied: they pointed game, guarded yards and caught moles and polecats, with smaller dogs once carried by bicycle to reach more trapping ground.
VBO:0201293.shortDescription: Affectionate but independent, the Stabijhoun pointed game, guarded Frisian yards, and caught moles and polecats.
VBO:0201293.historicalRoots: Versatile pointing and farm dog from the Frisian forest area of the Netherlands.

VBO:0201296.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terriers tend to be affectionate and playful with familiar people, bringing a warm social manner to everyday life. They also retain the courage and tenacity of their terrier ancestry; an intelligent, watchful dog can shift from play to focused attention when something around it changes.
VBO:0201296.shortDescription: Playful and affectionate with familiar people, the Staffordshire Bull Terrier retains terrier courage and watchfulness.

VBO:0201297.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, English is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201298.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Irish is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201299.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Miniature is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201300.summary: Staghound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201302.summary: A fast, keen hunter, the Stephens’ Cur often carries its head high while following a trail and has a strong instinct to mark quarry in trees. Hugh Stephens’s Kentucky family developed this distinct line from Mountain Cur stock. Its main work is hunting squirrel and raccoon, with packs also used for larger game.
VBO:0201302.shortDescription: A keen tree dog from Kentucky, known for following trails with its head high and hunting squirrel and raccoon.

VBO:0201305.summary: Tough and determined on a track, the Styrian Coarse-Haired Hound was developed for mountain hunting and wounded-game tracking. The breed traces to an 1870 cross arranged by Carl Peintinger in Styria; its rough weather-ready coat supports a hound known for giving tongue while working difficult terrain.
VBO:0201305.shortDescription: Tough and determined on mountain tracks, this Styrian hound gives tongue as it follows game.
VBO:0201305.historicalRoots: Developed in Styria from an 1870 Hanoverian Scent Hound–coarse-haired Istrian Hound cross selected for mountain work.

VBO:0201306.summary: Styrian Rough-Haired Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201307.summary: Styrian Wire-Haired Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201308.summary: Sussex Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201309.summary: Kindly in manner yet persistent on a scent, the Sussex Spaniel has a useful habit of giving voice while working thick cover. That call helps a hunter follow progress after the dog disappears into vegetation. The combination of steady determination and audible hunting sets it apart from quieter spaniels.
VBO:0201309.shortDescription: Kindly yet persistent on a scent, the Sussex Spaniel gives voice in thick cover so its hunter can follow.

VBO:0201310.summary: Swedish Briard is a variety of Briard.

VBO:0201311.summary: Swedish Cattle Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201315.summary: The Swedish Lapphund tends to be alert, affectionate and eager to engage with work; endurance and a ready response to training support its varied jobs. Sámi communities used it with reindeer, while northern households also valued it for hunting and watch duties. This range gave the breed a broader working history than herding alone.
VBO:0201315.shortDescription: Alert and affectionate, the Swedish Lapphund worked with Sámi reindeer and also took on hunting and watch duties.
VBO:0201315.historicalRoots: Sámi reindeer-herding, hunting and watch dog of Sweden.

VBO:0201316.summary: Alert, energetic and fearless, the Swedish Vallhund can work close to cattle heels with confidence around much larger animals. The breed survived on farms in West Gothland, where a 1940s search found remaining dogs and helped preserve an old Swedish herding tradition.
VBO:0201316.shortDescription: Alert and fearless, the Swedish Vallhund works close to cattle heels with confidence around much larger animals.

VBO:0201317.summary: Swedish White Elkhounds give a calm but alert impression, with energy and endurance behind a strong hunting drive. This Swedish hunting spitz developed from the gray Norwegian Elkhound and Jämthund lines, then gained Swedish Kennel Club recognition in 1993 as a distinct breed.
VBO:0201317.shortDescription: Calm-looking yet alert and energetic, this Swedish hunting spitz has a strong drive for game.
VBO:0201317.historicalRoots: Swedish hunting spitz derived from gray Norwegian Elkhound and Jämthund lines; recognized in 1993.

VBO:0201318.summary: Swiss Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Switzerland.

VBO:0201319.summary: Bernese Hounds are lively and passionately keen on hunting, yet sensitive and strongly attached to their handler. They follow hare, fox or roe deer independently while giving voice, and they search difficult ground with determination.
VBO:0201319.shortDescription: Lively and attached to its handler, this Bernese Hound follows scent independently and gives voice.
VBO:0201319.historicalRoots: Bernese variety of the Swiss Hound, with deep Swiss hunting roots.

VBO:0201320.summary: The Jura Hound is a keen, determined scent worker that can follow a trail independently and give voice as it goes. Like the other Swiss Hounds, it is also sensitive, docile and closely attached to its handler. Its tan-and-black coat marks the Jura variety of a breed long prized for hunting hare across difficult ground.
VBO:0201320.shortDescription: Determined on difficult scent trails, this tan-and-black Swiss hound keeps a close handler bond.
VBO:0201320.historicalRoots: Tan-and-black Jura variety of the Swiss Hound, used for hare and other quarry.

VBO:0201321.summary: Lucerne Hounds are lively and passionate about following scent, but sensitive and attached to their handlers. They can search independently with voice over difficult ground for hare and other quarry. Their blue-speckled coat with black patches and tan points sets this Swiss Hound variety apart within the shared working breed.
VBO:0201321.shortDescription: Lively and handler-attached, this blue-speckled Swiss hound follows difficult trails with voice.
VBO:0201321.historicalRoots: Blue-speckled Lucerne variety of the Swiss Hound, sharing its independent scent-hunting role.

VBO:0201322.summary: Schwyz Hounds share the Swiss Hound's lively interest in scent, sensitivity and attachment to their handlers. They hunt independently and give voice while searching difficult terrain. White with orange patches or an orange saddle, the Schwyz is one of four varieties brought under a single Swiss Hound standard in 1933.
VBO:0201322.shortDescription: Lively on scent yet sensitive with its handler, this orange-and-white Swiss hound hunts independently.
VBO:0201322.historicalRoots: Orange-and-white Schwyz variety of the Swiss Hound, unified under one standard in 1933.

VBO:0201323.summary: Swiss Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201324.summary: Swiss Short-Haired Pinscher is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201325.summary: Swiss White Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201327.summary: Sydney Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201328.summary: Tahitian Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201329.summary: Tahltan is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201331.summary: Persistent across broken highland ground, the Taigan can join coordinated Kyrgyz hunts with a golden eagle. National kennel accounts describe pursuit of fox, ibex, and other game at elevations that challenge many coursing dogs. Mountain stamina and that unusual partnership give the breed a distinct working story.
VBO:0201331.shortDescription: Persistent on highland hunts, the Taigan can pursue game alongside a Kyrgyz golden eagle.

VBO:0201333.summary: Talbot Hound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201334.summary: Tamaskan Dogs are generally friendly and outgoing, although some meet new people with a little reserve and can work independently. Their northern sled-dog heritage shows in an active, willing worker able to pull light loads at a moderate pace over short distances.
VBO:0201334.shortDescription: Friendly and willing to work, this northern sled-dog descendant may be reserved at first.
VBO:0201334.historicalRoots: Modern northern sled-dog-derived breed represented by the Tamaskan Dog Register.

VBO:0201335.summary: Tamaskan Husky is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201336.summary: Bred for loyalty, attentiveness and courage, the Tang Dog combines a lively character with watchfulness toward strangers. This southern Chinese watch and companion dog has a tradition of guarding homes and farms as well as hunting.
VBO:0201336.shortDescription: A lively southern Chinese watch and companion dog, bred for loyalty and courage, with a tradition of guarding and hunting.

VBO:0201337.summary: Tasy is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201338.summary: Tazy dogs are calm and self-possessed in ordinary life, then swift and keen when hunting. On Kazakhstan’s open land they have worked alone, in groups and alongside hunting birds, using both sight and scent to search for game. The breed appears in Kazakh tradition as one of the Seven Treasures, a reminder of its long connection to nomadic hunting life.
VBO:0201338.shortDescription: Calm at rest and keen in the field, the Tazy hunts across Kazakhstan’s open country with sight and scent.
VBO:0201338.historicalRoots: Kazakh sighthound of nomadic hunting culture, used alone, in groups and with hunting birds.

VBO:0201339.summary: Teacup Pomeranian is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201340.summary: Lively, alert and affectionate, the Teddy Roosevelt Terrier has a strong ratting and farm-work inheritance. The low-set, short-legged terrier is curious and often eager to join familiar people’s activities; historically it was known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier before adopting its present name.
VBO:0201340.shortDescription: Lively, affectionate and curious, this short-legged farm terrier has a long tradition of ratting work.
VBO:0201340.historicalRoots: An American short-legged ratting and farm terrier related to the Rat Terrier and formerly known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier.

VBO:0201341.summary: Telomian is a dog breed or regional type associated with Malaysia.

VBO:0201342.summary: The Tenterfield Terrier tends to be quick, agile and alert, traits once put to work against vermin around Australian farms. Small ratting terriers arrived with English settlers and became a distinct local type; later dogs also took part in tracking and earthdog sports. Its inquisitive nature links the old pest-control job to those newer activities.
VBO:0201342.shortDescription: Quick and inquisitive, the Tenterfield Terrier took on Australian farm vermin and later tracking and earthdog work.
VBO:0201342.interestingFact: The name honors Tenterfield saddler George Woolnough, whose terriers were known in the district.
VBO:0201342.historicalRoots: Australian farm and homestead vermin-control terrier.

VBO:0201343.summary: Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201346.summary: Tesem is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201347.summary: The Thai Bangkaew Dog is often alert, intelligent and loyal, with some reserve toward strangers. Its name comes from a village in Phitsanulok, where watchful household dogs developed a local identity; readiness to learn and respond to familiar people complements that guarding instinct.
VBO:0201347.shortDescription: Alert and loyal with familiar people, the Thai Bangkaew Dog carries a watchful household tradition from its namesake village.

VBO:0201348.summary: Thai Ridgebacks are active, resilient dogs with a strong attachment to their families and a remarkable talent for jumping. In eastern Thailand they hunted, kept watch and accompanied carts on journeys. Difficult travel between communities helped preserve the local dogs, giving the breed a history tied to everyday work as well as companionship.
VBO:0201348.shortDescription: Active and strongly attached to its people, the Thai Ridgeback hunted, watched, and traveled with carts in eastern Thailand.
VBO:0201348.historicalRoots: Long-established Thai ridged dog associated with eastern regions of the country.

VBO:0201349.summary: Tiara Teddy Bear is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201350.summary: Energetic and territorial, the Tibetan Kyi Apso was described by its breed club as keen on running but mellow off duty. Traditionally it guarded homes, monasteries and flocks with a deep warning bark. Daniel Taylor’s later memoir records that his import project ended because some dogs could be ferocious.
VBO:0201350.shortDescription: An energetic Tibetan guardian with a deep warning bark, described by its breed club as mellow when off duty.

VBO:0201351.summary: Protective of territory and closely loyal to familiar people, Tibetan Mastiffs tend to meet unfamiliar activity with serious watchfulness. Their Himalayan history includes guarding herds and monasteries, work that called for patience and independent judgment. The breed matures slowly; males may take four years or more to reach full development.
VBO:0201351.shortDescription: Territorial and loyal to familiar people, the Tibetan Mastiff guards with patience and independent judgment.

VBO:0201352.summary: The Tibetan Spaniel tends to be alert and loyal yet independent, sometimes aloof with strangers. Tibetan Spaniels served as both close companions and sentinels at Tibetan monasteries, watching from high walls and barking when something unusual approached. Its name is misleading: these were not European-style bird-flushing spaniels.
VBO:0201352.shortDescription: Alert and independent, the Tibetan Spaniel watched from monastery walls and barked at unusual arrivals.

VBO:0201353.summary: Lively and good-natured with familiar people, the Tibetan Terrier may be more reserved on a first meeting. It lived with Tibetan families, travelers and herders as a companion and watchful partner; despite the name, it is not a working earth terrier.
VBO:0201353.shortDescription: Lively with familiar people but sometimes reserved at first, the Tibetan Terrier was a companion and watchful travel partner.
VBO:0201353.historicalRoots: Tibetan herding, travel and companion dog.

VBO:0201354.summary: Titan Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201355.summary: Playful and energetic, the Tonya Finosu can combine companionship with watchfulness around the home. This regional dog is associated with Tonya and nearby parts of Trabzon on Turkey’s Black Sea coast. It has been kept to watch houses and the shelters and surroundings of farm animals.
VBO:0201355.shortDescription: A playful regional companion from Tonya, also kept to watch homes and farm-animal shelters.

VBO:0201356.summary: Calm and affectionate with familiar people, Tornjaks can become formidable when guarding entrusted livestock or property. In the mountains of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, they watched flocks and farmyards while keeping a careful eye on strangers. Modern breeders rebuilt the type from scattered survivors of that older pastoral tradition.
VBO:0201356.shortDescription: Calm and affectionate with familiar people, the Tornjak becomes resolute when guarding mountain flocks and farmyards.
VBO:0201356.interestingFact: Historical documents dated 1067 and 1374 mention dogs associated with the Tornjak’s region.
VBO:0201356.historicalRoots: Bosnian and Croatian mountain livestock protection.

VBO:0201357.summary: Composed and patient, the Tosa is known for quiet boldness. Bred in Japan’s Tosa region from Shikoku-ken and several Western breeds, it emerged from a historical fighting tradition; the FCI now recognizes its watchdog role.
VBO:0201357.shortDescription: Patient and composed yet bold, the Tosa is a Japanese mastiff whose role shifted from fighting to watching.
VBO:0201357.historicalRoots: Japanese molossoid developed in the Tosa region; historically used in dog fighting, now listed by FCI as watchdog.

VBO:0201358.summary: Friendly, alert and eager to please, the Toy American Eskimo Dog brings a quick-learning companion’s character to the breed’s smallest size. Its watchfulness includes barking at arrivals, and it can be conservative when meeting strangers. Toy Eskimos share one breed standard with the miniature and standard sizes.
VBO:0201358.shortDescription: An alert, eager-to-please toy companion, quick to learn and inclined to announce visitors with a warning bark.

VBO:0201359.summary: The American Stock Dog Registry describes its Toy Australian Shepherd as an intelligent, eager worker with a reserved streak around strangers. This is its 10–13.99-inch size variety, sharing a standard with larger Aussies. That standard emphasizes herding, agility and enthusiasm for assigned tasks.
VBO:0201359.shortDescription: An eager, attentive Aussie in the registry’s toy size, with shared herding ideals and reserve around strangers.

VBO:0201360.summary: Toy Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201361.summary: The Toy Fox Terrier tends to be quick and athletic, with an eagerness to learn that once brought some into circus performances. It grew from small Smooth Fox Terriers that proved useful as ratters on American farms. That mix of farm ratting, eager movement and trainable performance makes its history unusually varied.
VBO:0201361.shortDescription: Quick and eager to learn, the Toy Fox Terrier ranged from American farm ratting to circus performances.
VBO:0201361.historicalRoots: American small farm ratter developed from Smooth Fox Terrier stock.

VBO:0201363.summary: Toy Manchester Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201364.summary: Toy Rat Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201367.summary: Toy Trawler Spaniel is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201368.summary: Affectionate and playful, Trailhounds tend to have an independent streak and a strong pull toward interesting scents. Bred for speed and stamina in Cumbria’s hound-trailing races, they follow an artificial aniseed trail across fields and fells. Off duty, many enjoy curling up in a warm spot.
VBO:0201368.shortDescription: An affectionate, independent Cumbrian scent hound, bred to race over fields and fells and fond of a warm snooze.

VBO:0201371.summary: Alert and keen to hunt, the Treeing Cur finds game through sight, hearing and scent. It may give voice or stay quiet while tracking, with a distinct change when quarry reaches a tree. Rural American breeders selected these versatile dogs for performance, combining hunting with guarding and livestock work.
VBO:0201371.shortDescription: An alert tree dog using sight, hearing and scent, with voice on the trail varying between individuals.

VBO:0201372.summary: Highly alert, the Treeing Feist hunts through both sight and scent and tends to remain almost silent while following a trail. Generations of performance breeding in the rural American South shaped its small-game work. Squirrel hunting remains central, with raccoon, opossum, rabbits and flushing game birds also among its uses.
VBO:0201372.shortDescription: An alert, usually quiet tracker using sight and scent, with squirrel hunting central to its working history.

VBO:0201373.summary: Intelligent, alert and companionable in its UKC standard, the Treeing Tennessee Brindle is a scent hunter with a strong instinct to tree game. Its voice marks the work: it calls along the trail, then changes its bark at the tree, where a coarse, repeated chop is preferred.
VBO:0201373.shortDescription: An alert, companionable scent hunter that trees game and changes its voice when the trail reaches the tree.

VBO:0201374.summary: Active, alert and intelligent, the Treeing Walker Coonhound can stay with a raccoon scent deep into a night hunt. It signals from the base of a tree when quarry is located, using its characteristic voice to guide a hunter to the end of a trail that may be out of sight.
VBO:0201374.shortDescription: Active and alert, the Treeing Walker follows raccoon scent through night hunts and voices when quarry is treed.

VBO:0201375.summary: Haiden C. Trigg prized speed, scenting ability and the willingness to range in his foxhounds. He described running red foxes to earth or catching them and wrote that feeding the pack himself helped him gain their affection. His Kentucky strain grew from Birdsong and Maupin dogs; a 2000 keeper account describes Trigg hounds competing in organized hunts.
VBO:0201375.shortDescription: Trigg valued speed, scenting ability and ranging in his Kentucky foxhounds, whose keeper accounts describe pack hunts.

VBO:0201377.summary: Turnspit Dog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201378.summary: Tweed Water Spaniel is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201379.summary: Steady and driven by scent, the Tyrolean Hound searches independently and calls as it follows a trail. This Austrian woodland and mountain hunter works on hare and fox and tracks wounded game. A keen nose and strong sense of direction support its persistent work.
VBO:0201379.shortDescription: A steady, independent Austrian scent hound known for persistent trail work and a clear tracking voice.

VBO:0201380.summary: Intelligent, according to Utonagan Society contributor Nadia Carlyle, these dogs came from a British breeding project begun in the 1980s. Her 2005 account records Mahtal Iskote at Carrara appearing in the Crufts Good Citizens’ ring for the Pets as Therapy parade. The society was also organizing breeder support and a rescue network.
VBO:0201380.shortDescription: Utonagan were described as intelligent, with a recorded 2005 Pets as Therapy parade appearance at Crufts.

VBO:0201381.summary: Gos Rater Valencià dogs are lively and affectionate with familiar people, while keeping a watchful reserve around strangers. Valencian farms valued their quick warning bark and their persistence against rats, moles and rabbits. The breed’s rise coincided with orange growing in the region; its small working build let it move through cultivated fields and farm edges.
VBO:0201381.shortDescription: Lively and affectionate with familiar people, this small Valencian farm dog warns quickly and pursues pests.
VBO:0201381.historicalRoots: Valencian farm ratter and alert dog associated with nineteenth-century orange-growing country.

VBO:0201382.summary: Valley Bulldogs tend to combine an outgoing, playful character with a protective streak. Their history centers on farm and ranch work, from managing cattle and other unruly livestock to guarding the property. Thought to have emerged in Nova Scotia’s Annapolis Valley, the breed developed through generations of selected Boxer and Bulldog ancestry.
VBO:0201382.shortDescription: An outgoing, playful farm dog with a protective streak, developed through selected Boxer and Bulldog ancestry.

VBO:0201383.summary: Verelade is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201384.summary: Confidence, loyalty and watchfulness are emphasized in the Victorian Bulldog registry standard. It allows well-socialized mature dogs to show more composure and reserve around neutral strangers. This modern English breeding project traces to Ken Mollett in the 1980s, with a later association formed to preserve it.
VBO:0201384.shortDescription: A modern English bulldog program whose registry standard emphasizes confidence, loyalty and mature composure.

VBO:0201385.summary: Vikhan is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201387.summary: Lively and responsive with its owner, the Villano de las Encartaciones can be cautious and reserved with unfamiliar people. Its working role calls for strength and decisiveness in handling cattle. Farmers in the Encartaciones region traditionally used these dogs to catch semi-wild Monchina cattle on the mountainsides.
VBO:0201387.shortDescription: A responsive cattle-handling dog from the Encartaciones, often reserved with unfamiliar people.

VBO:0201388.summary: Quick to announce unfamiliar sounds and affectionate with their people, Villanucos were described by Mariano Gómez Fernández as farm companions in Bizkaia’s Encartaciones district. His account records rodent and small-game hunting, and dogs that accompanied the larger Villano before cattle were caught.
VBO:0201388.shortDescription: Mariano Gómez Fernández described an affectionate Encartaciones farm companion, quick to alert and historically used for ratting.

VBO:0201389.summary: Friendly and eager to learn, the Vizsla tends to keep close contact with its handler through a hunt. It finds game, holds a point, and retrieves across Hungarian fields, forests, and water. That constant human partnership is one of its distinctive habits, grounded in a sporting history that reaches back through Magyar hunting traditions.
VBO:0201389.shortDescription: Friendly and eager to learn, the Vizsla stays close to its handler while finding, pointing, and retrieving game.
VBO:0201389.interestingFact: Hungarian documents and illustrations depicting the type reach back to the fourteenth century.
VBO:0201389.historicalRoots: Hungarian versatile pointing and retrieving dog.

VBO:0201390.summary: The Volpino Italiano tends to be lively and playful, closely attached to its people. It has long lived in both Italian noble houses and ordinary homes, serving as companion and alert little watchdog. Eighteenth-century carters in Tuscany and Latium valued the breed for announcing strangers along the road.
VBO:0201390.shortDescription: Lively and playful, the Volpino Italiano stayed close to people and announced strangers for traveling Italian carters.
VBO:0201390.interestingFact: A Volpino appears in a Venetian painting by Vittore Carpaccio dated 1502.
VBO:0201390.historicalRoots: Italian household watchdog and companion with European spitz roots.

VBO:0201391.summary: Vucciriscu is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201394.summary: Friendly and open, though sometimes reserved on first meeting, the Waller is described by its breed association as an intelligent dog that enjoys work. The association gives it a broad role spanning family life, sport and herding. Its standard favors quick, flexible movement rather than a heavy build.
VBO:0201394.shortDescription: A friendly, work-loving dog whose association describes family, sport and herding roles, with some initial reserve.

VBO:0201396.summary: Water Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201397.summary: Water Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201401.summary: Steady and persistent, the Weimaraner brings a strong nose and watchful attention to hunting work. It searches for game, points and follows up after the shot on land or water; its early development is closely associated with the German court of Weimar.
VBO:0201401.shortDescription: Steady and persistent, the Weimaraner searches, points, and follows up after the shot on land or water.
VBO:0201401.historicalRoots: German versatile pointing and retrieving dog.

VBO:0201402.summary: Long-haired Weimaraners share the breed’s steady, scent-driven hunting character: they search methodically, point game and work in water as well as on land. The long-haired variety has been recorded since the turn of the twentieth century, after the breed’s nineteenth-century development around Weimar and Thuringia.
VBO:0201402.shortDescription: A steady, methodical scent hunter, the long-haired Weimaraner points game and works on land and in water.

VBO:0201403.summary: Weimaraners are steady yet passionate hunting dogs, known for methodical searching and keen scenting. They were kept at the Weimar court by the early 1800s; professional hunters and gamekeepers then shaped the breed across central Germany. The shorthaired variety was established before the rarer longhaired form appeared around the turn of the 20th century.
VBO:0201403.shortDescription: Steady yet keen on a scent, this shorthaired German pointer traces its story to the Weimar court.
VBO:0201403.historicalRoots: German versatile pointing and hunting dog

VBO:0201406.summary: Welsh Corgi is a dog breed or regional type associated with Wales and United Kingdom.

VBO:0201408.summary: Welsh Hillman is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201409.summary: Independent and self-reliant, the Welsh Hound is a hunter shaped by rugged, rocky country. It follows low scent and uses a talkative voice that carries across windy Welsh hills. Organized hunts have maintained packs of these native hounds through a long regional hunting tradition.
VBO:0201409.shortDescription: An independent Welsh pack hound, shaped by rocky hills and known for a carrying, talkative voice.

VBO:0201410.summary: Welsh Sheepdogs use their own initiative to move livestock across open hill country, while also taking direction from a handler. Their herding and guarding instincts reach back to drovers’ dogs that kept cattle and sheep together on long routes. The Welsh Sheepdog Society has worked since 1997 to preserve this native working strain.
VBO:0201410.shortDescription: An independent Welsh hill-country herder that also takes direction and watches over livestock.
VBO:0201410.historicalRoots: Welsh farm and droving dogs; preservation through the Welsh Sheepdog Society since 1997.

VBO:0201411.summary: Active and merry, Welsh Springer Spaniels tend to be kindly with familiar people and persistent when searching cover. They flush game through rough vegetation in a Welsh sporting tradition separate from the English Springer’s. That patient, lively search is a distinctive skill behind their familiar companion manner.
VBO:0201411.shortDescription: Merry and kind with familiar people, the Welsh Springer persists through rough cover to flush game.

VBO:0201412.summary: The Welsh Terrier tends to be game and fearless, with an affectionate, tractable side in close company. It once hunted fox, badger and even otter, requiring persistence with challenging quarry. Its old work called for a dog willing to press on underground and stay responsive to its handler.
VBO:0201412.shortDescription: Fearless on difficult quarry yet affectionate in company, the Welsh Terrier pursued fox, badger, and otter.
VBO:0201412.historicalRoots: Welsh fox, badger and otter working terrier.

VBO:0201414.summary: West Country Harrier is a dog breed or regional type associated with England and United Kingdom.

VBO:0201415.summary: Alert, cheerful and self-reliant, the West Highland White Terrier keeps the courage of its Scottish hunting ancestry. Terriers from the Poltalloch area pursued quarry and controlled vermin around rough-country farms; the lively readiness to investigate remains a central part of its character.
VBO:0201415.shortDescription: Cheerful and self-reliant, the Westie keeps the courage and curiosity of Scottish rough-country vermin work.

VBO:0201416.summary: West Siberian Laikas are steady and alert, self-confident around strangers and intensely interested in hunting. In forest work, they use a keen nose to seek both feathered and furred game. The breed grew from Khanty and Mansi hunting dogs in the Ural and Siberian forests.
VBO:0201416.shortDescription: Steady and alert, this laika uses a keen nose to seek both feathered and furred game in forest work.

VBO:0201417.summary: A Westiepoo named Doctor Ted has a regular visiting role at Great Ormond Street Hospital. He joined the volunteer team in February 2022 and visits children’s physiotherapy classes; away from work, he enjoys walks and garden patrols with another dog.
VBO:0201417.shortDescription: The Westie–Poodle cross has a documented hospital visiting role through a dog called Doctor Ted.

VBO:0201418.summary: Westphalian Dachsbrackes are friendly, adaptable hunters with a fine nose and a strong passion for following a track. Pure breeding of these smaller, low-running hounds began in the 1880s as hunting grounds shrank; they kept the working role of the German Bracke in a sturdier, short-legged frame.
VBO:0201418.shortDescription: A friendly, track-focused small hound developed for the tighter hunting grounds of Westphalia.
VBO:0201418.historicalRoots: Westphalian small running hound developed in the 1880s for smaller hunting grounds.

VBO:0201419.summary: Self-willed and watchful around the house, the Wetterhoun can be affectionate with familiar people yet reserved toward strangers. Around Friesland’s waterways it hunted otters and other small predators while also guarding the yard. Its local history even includes pulling small carts in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
VBO:0201419.shortDescription: Self-willed and watchful, the Wetterhoun hunted around Frisian waterways while guarding the yard.
VBO:0201419.historicalRoots: Frisian water hunting and farmyard work.

VBO:0201420.summary: Wheaten Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201421.summary: Whippets are often gentle, affectionate companions at home, with a very different intensity when something sets off their urge to chase. In northern England, working people developed them for small-game hunting and weekend racing. A favorite contest sent the dogs sprinting toward their owners, who waved a rag at the finish line.
VBO:0201421.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate at home, the Whippet turns intensely focused when the urge to chase takes hold.
VBO:0201421.interestingFact: Modern lure coursing gives Whippets an outlet for their pursuit instinct by sending them after an artificial lure.
VBO:0201421.historicalRoots: British sighthound developed for racing and small-game coursing.

VBO:0201422.summary: Poised and self-confident, the White Shepherd tends to be open and friendly with familiar people while watching strangers more reservedly. Its breed standard describes both herding and protective instincts, alongside an eagerness to respond when needed. Maintained by breeders who continued the white shepherd lines, this American breed gained separate United Kennel Club recognition in 1999.
VBO:0201422.shortDescription: Poised with familiar people and observant of strangers, the White Shepherd retains herding and protective instincts.

VBO:0201423.summary: The White Swiss Shepherd Dog tends to be balanced and friendly, attentive to its people and often quick to learn. Its modern role includes companionship and sport, with an eagerness for activity that carries into both. White shepherd lines were maintained in North America before Swiss breeders established the breed from the 1970s.
VBO:0201423.shortDescription: Balanced and friendly, the White Swiss Shepherd stays attentive to its people and eager for activity and sport.
VBO:0201423.interestingFact: A North American male named Lobo, born in 1966, is cited as a progenitor of the Swiss population.
VBO:0201423.historicalRoots: North American white shepherd ancestry established as a Swiss breed.

VBO:0201424.summary: The Wire Fox Terrier is often alert, curious and fearless, yet friendly and forthcoming with people. Its quick reactions served active fox work, where a dog had to keep investigating when quarry vanished underground; that blend of nerve and sociability remains its signature.
VBO:0201424.shortDescription: Alert and curious yet friendly with people, the Wire Fox Terrier investigates when quarry disappears underground.

VBO:0201425.summary: Wire Haired Whippet is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201426.summary: Lively, alert and quietly confident in the breed standard, the Wire-Haired Jack Russell shares the working character of the breed’s other coat varieties. Its ancestors ran with foxhounds and went below ground to flush quarry. John Russell developed that terrier strain in England in the nineteenth century.
VBO:0201426.shortDescription: An alert, quietly confident rough-coated Jack Russell, with a history of following foxhounds and flushing quarry.

VBO:0201427.summary: Keenly attentive in the field and closely attached to familiar people, the Wirehaired Pointing Griffon also keeps watch over its territory. Eduard Korthals refined the breed as a versatile hunter that could point game and follow wounded larger quarry. Its broad field skills grew alongside that strong human partnership.
VBO:0201427.shortDescription: Attentive in the field and attached to its people, the Griffon points game and follows wounded quarry.

VBO:0201428.summary: The Wirehaired Vizsla tends to be affectionate and sensitive to rough handling, while retaining a keen hunting drive. It likes to stay in contact with its handler, search for game and hold a firm point. Hungarian breeders developed it in the 1930s for the older Vizsla’s versatile hunting role across rougher field conditions.
VBO:0201428.shortDescription: Affectionate and sensitive, the Wirehaired Vizsla stays in touch with its handler while searching and pointing.
VBO:0201428.historicalRoots: Hungarian versatile pointing dog created in the 1930s.

VBO:0201431.summary: Wolfhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201433.summary: Happy, athletic and energetic in breeder Roz Wardrop’s account, the Working Cocker Spaniel brings a strong hunting drive to its handler’s work. Working lines are selected for intelligence, speed and hunting style rather than coat colour. Finding and flushing game is their central job, from rabbits to pheasants.
VBO:0201433.shortDescription: A happy, energetic working Cocker, selected for hunting style and speed and bred to find and flush game.

VBO:0201434.summary: Working Kelpies are alert, eager stock dogs bred to manage sheep in open country and in yards, then settle between jobs. Their work calls for smooth, economical movement and the judgment to solve problems as a flock shifts. The working strain is selected around ability in the field, a different emphasis from the show Kelpie's appearance standard.
VBO:0201434.shortDescription: Alert and eager around stock, this Australian working strain is valued for judgment and smooth, tireless movement.
VBO:0201434.historicalRoots: Australian working Kelpie stock-dog strain selected for sheep work across open country and yards.

VBO:0201435.summary: Xiasi dogs from Guizhou have long been valued locally for a keen nose, speed and courage in hunting, along with watchfulness at home. The tradition is still active: selected dogs have recently entered formal police-dog training, carrying a regional working skill into a new setting.
VBO:0201435.shortDescription: Locally valued for courage and a keen nose, Xiasi dogs hunted in Guizhou and kept watch at home.

VBO:0201436.summary: Xoloitzcuintlis tend to be calm and fairly quiet, yet attentive to unfamiliar arrivals and sometimes reserved with strangers. Their companionship has deep roots in Mexican culture: in pre-Hispanic belief, these dogs were associated with Xolotl and guided the souls of the dead on their onward journey. The breed’s story combines everyday watchfulness with an extraordinary spiritual role.
VBO:0201436.shortDescription: Calm and quiet but watchful of arrivals, the Xolo also carries a deep role in pre-Hispanic Mexican belief.
VBO:0201436.historicalRoots: Ancient Mexican dog represented in pre-Columbian culture and modern hairless and coated forms.

VBO:0201437.summary: Intermediate Xoloitzcuintles share the breed's quiet, calm manner, cheerful alertness and tendency to watch strangers carefully. The Mexican standard assigns the intermediate size a watchdog role. This native breed came close to disappearing before the Mexican Kennel Club helped restore it and adopted its image as a logo in 1940.
VBO:0201437.shortDescription: A calm, watchful Mexican dog whose native breed was rescued from near extinction.
VBO:0201437.historicalRoots: Ancient Mexican native breed preserved after a period of near extinction; Mexican Kennel Club logo since 1940.

VBO:0201438.summary: Miniature Xoloitzcuintles are generally quiet and calm, yet cheerful and alert; they may be reserved with strangers. The FCI classifies the miniature size as a companion, while the larger sizes have a watchdog role. This small hairless form belongs to a Mexican breed whose history reaches back to pre-Hispanic times.
VBO:0201438.shortDescription: A quiet, alert miniature Mexican companion from the Xoloitzcuintle’s ancient lineage.
VBO:0201438.historicalRoots: Pre-Hispanic Mexican Xoloitzcuintle lineage; FCI miniature companion variety.

VBO:0201439.summary: Standard Xoloitzcuintles are quiet, alert companions whose watchful reserve toward strangers suits the standard size's watchdog role. The breed has deep roots in pre-Hispanic Mexico, where it appeared in ritual belief as a guide for souls. It later became scarce, and the Mexican Kennel Club helped preserve it in the twentieth century.
VBO:0201439.shortDescription: A quiet, alert Mexican watchdog with a long place in pre-Hispanic ritual tradition.
VBO:0201439.historicalRoots: Pre-Hispanic Mexican ritual tradition; preservation by the Mexican Kennel Club.

VBO:0201440.summary: Xoloitzcuintli, Toy is a variety of Xoloitzcuintli.

VBO:0201441.summary: Yajivy is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201442.summary: Bold and energetic at work, Yakutian Laikas are also described as friendly and sociable with people. Communities of northeastern Russia relied on them as sled dogs and hunting partners through severe Arctic conditions. That joining of endurance and close human partnership has carried through a long regional history.
VBO:0201442.shortDescription: Bold at work and sociable with people, Yakutian Laikas partnered in Arctic sled travel and hunting.

VBO:0201443.summary: Yellow Black Mouth Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201444.summary: Spunky and agile in a firsthand account, Emma offers a glimpse of the Yo-Chon, a Bichon Frise–Yorkshire Terrier cross. At 14 months she was described as full-grown and keen to jump over obstacles, though she stayed on a lead because she would run off. A separate encounter records her caution around a larger Boxer puppy; her owners reported that she played with a neighbour’s adult Golden Retriever.
VBO:0201444.shortDescription: A Bichon Frise–Yorkshire Terrier cross; adult Emma’s firsthand accounts record jumping and caution around a larger puppy.

VBO:0201445.summary: Affectionate with his owner, three-year-old Chico was a Yorkshire Terrier–Pomeranian cross. Líria Rodrigues described him sneaking into bedrooms to steal socks for play and sleeping close beside her. She also reported a less welcome habit: he liked biting visitors’ heels.
VBO:0201445.shortDescription: Chico’s owner described a Yorkshire Terrier–Pomeranian cross fond of sock-stealing play and sleeping close beside her.

VBO:0201446.summary: Yorkie Russell is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201447.summary: Zoey, a Yorkipoo with Comfort Caring Canines, enjoys fetch, new toys and snuggling. She became a therapy dog in September 2016. Another Yorkipoo, Leah, made weekly visits to Soin Medical Center before the pandemic and appeared in a 2019 video about therapy animals.
VBO:0201447.shortDescription: Named Yorkipoos show different activities: Zoey enjoys fetch and snuggling; Leah made hospital visits.

VBO:0201448.summary: The Yorkshire Terrier tends to be alert and spirited while keeping an even disposition. It emerged from nineteenth-century English terrier lines with an instinct for chasing rodents, later becoming a close companion. The quick attention to movement behind that original job remains part of its familiar terrier character.
VBO:0201448.shortDescription: Alert and spirited, the Yorkshire Terrier still notices movement quickly, echoing its English rodent-chasing roots.
VBO:0201448.historicalRoots: Yorkshire terrier developed in the mid-nineteenth century from several small terrier lines.

VBO:0201449.summary: Miniature Yorkshire Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201450.summary: Yugoslavian Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201452.summary: Local keepers describe Zerdavas as strongly attached to their owners, with an enduring place in hunting and guarding. In the eastern Black Sea mountains, traditional hunters use them as barking pointers, generally tracking quietly before giving voice when quarry is found. Wild boar is an important part of that regional working history.
VBO:0201452.shortDescription: A devoted regional hunting and guard dog, traditionally used as a barking pointer in the Black Sea mountains.

VBO:0201453.summary: de Pont-Audemer Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201454.summary: The German Pinscher is typically lively, intelligent and self-assured, with the evenness to stay engaged through a day's activity. It carries an old farm-watchdog tradition; early smooth Pinschers and rough-coated Schnauzers came from the same stock, before their paths separated.
VBO:0201454.shortDescription: Lively and self-assured, the German Pinscher brings even attention to activity and an old farm-watchdog tradition.
VBO:0201454.historicalRoots: German smooth-coated watch and companion dog.

VBO:0201455.summary: The French Bulldog tends to be lively, playful and sociable, eager to stay involved with its people. It took shape among Parisian porters, butchers and coachmen before finding favor in the city’s artistic and social circles. The Paris street-to-salon path is part of its distinct story.
VBO:0201455.shortDescription: Playful and sociable, the French Bulldog stays involved with its people, a companion shaped in Parisian working circles.
VBO:0201455.historicalRoots: Parisian companion dog developed in the late nineteenth century.

VBO:0201456.summary: Sangsari is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201457.summary: Cane da Pastore D'Oropa is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201458.summary: Reserved with strangers and closely attached to familiar people, the Cane di Mannara tends to be calm around the animals in its care. Sicilian farms used it to guard the mannara, or sheepfold, and the flock sheltered there. Its protective work has continued against threats such as foxes and free-roaming dogs.
VBO:0201458.shortDescription: An attached but reserved Sicilian guardian, traditionally watching sheepfolds and the flocks in its care.

VBO:0201459.summary: Lively and steadfast in guarding, the Pastore della Sila is strongly attached to its shepherd. It can be more receptive to unfamiliar people when that trusted person is present. The breed developed in Calabria’s rugged mountains, where protecting livestock, especially goats, from wolves shaped its working life.
VBO:0201459.shortDescription: A devoted Calabrian livestock guardian, shaped by mountain work protecting flocks and goats.

VBO:0201460.summary: Steadfast and tireless in its guarding role, the Spino degli Iblei is closely tied to the flock it protects. It may accept unfamiliar people more readily when the shepherd is present. For centuries, breeders in southeastern Sicily’s Hyblaean Mountains have selected these dogs to defend sheep and goats, keeping that work central to the breed.
VBO:0201460.shortDescription: A steadfast Sicilian flock guardian, bred in the Hyblaean Mountains to protect sheep and goats.

VBO:0201461.summary: The Cane Lupino del Gigante’s association describes strong attachment to a familiar handler. Agile and enduring, this local “Luvin” traditionally moved flocks and cattle across the steep Reggio Emilia Apennines. Preservation work began in 1997, followed by a dedicated association in 2009.
VBO:0201461.shortDescription: An agile, enduring Apennine flock dog, described by its association as strongly attached to a familiar handler.

VBO:0201462.summary: Reserved with strangers and quietly affectionate with familiar people, Levriero Meridionale are described by conservation breeder Flaviano Bruno as sensitive hounds closely attached to their household or pack. This southern Italian working sighthound was selected for hunting hares by sight, combining swift pursuit with sustained effort.
VBO:0201462.shortDescription: Southern Italian working sighthounds, described as reserved with strangers, gently affectionate and persistent in hare pursuit.

VBO:0201463.summary: Quick in pursuit, the Xigou belongs to China’s local sighthound traditions. In Shaanxi’s Guanzhong region, keepers described seasonal hare coursing around Pucheng and Fuping, crossing open farmland with their dogs. CKU documented living Shaanxi dogs through identification and registration in Xi’an in 2017.
VBO:0201463.shortDescription: A regional Chinese sighthound with a tradition of seasonal hare coursing in Shaanxi’s open farmland.

VBO:0201464.summary: Tarsus çatalburun is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201465.summary: Chihuahua - Teacup is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201487.summary: Confidence, zest for life and eagerness to please their family are the traits emphasized in the American Bully standard. The Pocket variety follows that companion standard in a shorter dog, with size determined by adult height and the same breed type and build.
VBO:0201487.shortDescription: The American Bully’s companion ideal in a shorter variety, defined by adult height rather than a different build.
